at bade.explanation: "At bade" means "to bathe or swim". When you go into the sea or a lake, say "Vi bader i havet" (We swim in the sea). Do not mix it up with "at svømme" (to swim): "Hun svømmer hver morgen" (She swims every morning).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bade** i havet i dag.
sentence.en: We would like to swim in the sea today.

at bagatellisere.explanation: "At bagatellisere" means "to downplay". It comes from "en bagatel" (a trifle). To say it is wrong to treat something serious as small, say "Man må ikke bagatellisere vold" (You must not downplay violence).

sentence.da: Politikerne vil **bagatellisere** problemet, men det er alvorligt.
sentence.en: The politicians want to downplay the problem, but it is serious.

at bage.explanation: "At bage" means "to bake". To say what you bake, put the thing after the verb: "Vi bager brød i weekenden" (We bake bread at the weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bage** en kage i ovnen.
sentence.en: I want to bake a cake in the oven.

at bakke op.explanation: "At bakke op" means "to back up or support". When you say which person or decision you support, put "om" (about) after "op": "Vi bakker op om hendes forslag" (We back up her proposal).

sentence.da: Hele klassen vil **bakke op** om læreren.
sentence.en: The whole class will back up the teacher.

at balancere.explanation: "At balancere" means "to balance". When you find the right mix between two things, say "Hun balancerer arbejde og familie" (She balances work and family).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **balancere** på en smal bom.
sentence.en: The children can balance on a narrow beam.

at bande.explanation: "At bande" means "to swear (curse)". Do not mix it up with "at sværge" (to swear a promise): "Jeg sværger, at jeg siger sandheden" (I swear that I am telling the truth).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **bande** foran børnene.
sentence.en: You must not swear in front of the children.

at banke på.explanation: "At banke på" means "to knock". When you knock on something, "på" (on) must follow the verb: "Han banker på døren" (He knocks on the door). Without "på", "at banke" is also used for a heart: "Hjertet banker" (The heart pounds).

sentence.da: Du skal **banke på**, når døren er lukket.
sentence.en: You have to knock when the door is closed.

at barbere.explanation: "At barbere" means "to shave". Add "sig" (yourself) when you shave yourself: "Han barberer sig hver morgen" (He shaves every morning). Without "sig", you shave someone or something else: "Lægen barberer området før operationen" (The doctor shaves the area before the surgery).

sentence.da: Med en barbermaskine kan man **barbere** sit skæg af på få minutter.
sentence.en: With an electric shaver you can shave off your beard in a few minutes.

at barbere sig.explanation: "At barbere sig" means "to shave". It is built from "at barbere" (to shave) and "sig" (yourself). When you talk about "he", "sig" stays as it is: "Han barberer sig hver morgen" (He shaves every morning). To shave someone else, leave "sig" out: "Jeg barberer ham" (I shave him).

sentence.da: Han har skæg og vil **barbere sig**.
sentence.en: He has a beard and wants to shave.

at bearbejde.explanation: "At bearbejde" means "to process or work on". It is built from "at arbejde" (to work). When you deal with something hard in your feelings, say "Hun bearbejder sin sorg" (She is processing her grief).

sentence.da: Snedkeren skal **bearbejde** træet og bygge et skab.
sentence.en: The carpenter must work the wood and build a cabinet.

at bebo.explanation: "At bebo" means "to inhabit". It is built from "at bo" (to live). "At bo" needs "i" (in) before the place: "Familien bor i huset" (The family lives in the house). "At bebo" takes the place directly: "Familien bebor huset" (The family inhabits the house).

sentence.da: Kun få kan **bebo** den lille ø om vinteren.
sentence.en: Only a few can inhabit the small island in winter.

at bebrejde.explanation: "At bebrejde" means "to blame". When you blame yourself, say "Jeg bebrejder mig selv" (I blame myself). To name the mistake you blame the person for, add "for" (for): "Hun bebrejder ham for fejlen" (She blames him for the mistake).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **bebrejde** ham, at han var bange.
sentence.en: You cannot blame him for being scared.

at bede.explanation: "At bede" means "to ask or pray". When you ask someone to do something, say "Jeg bad hende om at komme" (I asked her to come). When you pray, say "Hun beder til Gud" (She prays to God). Do not mix it up with "at spørge" (to ask a question): "Jeg spørger ham, hvad klokken er" (I ask him what time it is).

sentence.da: Må jeg **bede** dig om hjælp?
sentence.en: May I ask you for help?

at bede om.explanation: "At bede om" means "to ask for". It is built from "at bede" (to ask / pray) and "om" (for). When you ask politely for something in a café, say "Må jeg bede om regningen?" (May I ask for the bill?). Do not mix it up with "at spørge" (to ask a question): "Jeg spørger om vejen" (I ask about the way).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bede om** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to ask for a cup of coffee.

at bedrage.explanation: "At bedrage" means "to deceive". When someone is unfaithful to a partner, it means "to cheat on": "Han bedrog hende" (He cheated on her).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **bedrage** kunderne med falske tilbud.
sentence.en: You must not deceive the customers with false offers.

at bedømme.explanation: "At bedømme" means "to judge or assess". It is built from "at dømme" (to sentence). When you ask someone to assess a danger, say "Kan du bedømme risikoen?" (Can you assess the risk?). Do not mix it up with "at dømme" (to sentence), which is the word used in court: "Retten dømmer manden til fængsel" (The court sentences the man to prison).

sentence.da: Dommerne skal **bedømme** kagerne i konkurrencen.
sentence.en: The judges must judge the cakes in the contest.

at befinde sig.explanation: "At befinde sig" means "to be (located)". When you say where people are, "sig" changes to match them: "Vi befinder os i Aarhus" (We are in Aarhus). Do not mix it up with "at være" (to be): "Hvor er du?" (Where are you?)

sentence.da: Hotellet skal **befinde sig** tæt på stranden, fordi vi vil bade.
sentence.en: The hotel has to be near the beach, because we want to swim.

at befri.explanation: "At befri" means "to free or liberate". It is built from "fri" (free). When you free someone from a worry, add "for" (from) before the worry: "Pengene befrier ham for bekymringer" (The money frees him from worries).

sentence.da: Soldaterne vil **befri** fangerne fra fængslet.
sentence.en: The soldiers will free the prisoners from the prison.

at begejstre.explanation: "At begejstre" means "to thrill or excite". When something makes people enthusiastic, that thing is the subject: "Filmen begejstrer børnene" (The film thrills the children). Do not mix it up with "spændt" (excited, eager), which says how you yourself feel: "Jeg er spændt på resultatet" (I am excited about the result).

sentence.da: Hendes tale kan **begejstre** hele salen.
sentence.en: Her speech can thrill the whole room.

at begrave.explanation: "At begrave" means "to bury". When you drop an idea for good, say "De begravede planen" (They buried the plan).

sentence.da: Piraterne vil **begrave** skatten på en øde ø.
sentence.en: The pirates will bury the treasure on a deserted island.

at begrunde.explanation: "At begrunde" means "to justify". It is built from "en grund" (a reason). When someone asks you to back up an answer, say "Kan du begrunde dit svar?" (Can you justify your answer?)

sentence.da: Du skal **begrunde** din mening med gode eksempler.
sentence.en: You must justify your opinion with good examples.

at begrænse.explanation: "At begrænse" means "to limit". It is built from "en grænse" (a border). When you limit yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Jeg begrænser mig til én kop kaffe" (I limit myself to one cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **begrænse** brugen af mobiltelefoner i timerne.
sentence.en: The school wants to limit the use of cell phones in class.

at begunstige.explanation: "At begunstige" means "to favor". It is built from "en gunst" (a favor). When a rule helps one group more than another, say "Loven begunstiger store firmaer" (The law favors big companies).

sentence.da: Skatten vil **begunstige** familier med børn.
sentence.en: The tax will favor families with children.

at begynde.explanation: "At begynde" means "to begin". To say what you begin to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read). To say when something starts, use it alone: "Kurset begynder i januar" (The course begins in January).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **begynde** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The movie is going to begin at eight.

at begynde på.explanation: "At begynde på" means "to begin on". When you start a job, say "Han begynder på et nyt arbejde i morgen" (He begins a new job tomorrow). When a verb follows, use "at begynde" without "på": "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read).

sentence.da: Efter ferien skal jeg **begynde på** universitetet.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am going to start at the university.

at begå.explanation: "At begå" means "to commit (a crime)". It also goes with mistakes. To say someone made a mistake, say "Han begik en fejl" (He made a mistake). With "sig" (yourself) it has a different meaning, "to get by": "Hun kan begå sig på fransk" (She can get by in French).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **begå** endnu et indbrud i nat.
sentence.en: The thief will commit another break-in tonight.

at behandle.explanation: "At behandle" means "to treat". When you talk about how someone acts toward a person, say "Han behandler mig godt" (He treats me well). When an office deals with a case, it means "to handle": "Kommunen behandler sagen" (The city is handling the case).

sentence.da: Lægen kan **behandle** sygdommen med medicin.
sentence.en: The doctor can treat the illness with medicine.

at beherske.explanation: "At beherske" means "to master or control". It is built from "at herske" (to rule). When you keep your feelings under control, add "sig" (oneself): "Han kunne ikke beherske sig" (He could not control himself).

sentence.da: Hun kan **beherske** tre sprog og taler dem flydende.
sentence.en: She has a good command of three languages and speaks them fluently.

at beholde.explanation: "At beholde" means "to keep". It is built from "at holde" (to hold). When you keep a promise, use "at holde" and not "at beholde": "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **beholde** bogen.
sentence.en: You may keep the book.

at behøve.explanation: "At behøve" means "to need". To ask whether something has to be done, say "Behøver jeg at skrive under?" (Do I need to sign?) A very common phrase for needing a thing is "at have brug for" (to need): "Jeg har brug for hjælp" (I need help).

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **behøve** at betale.
sentence.en: You will not need to pay.

at bekende.explanation: "At bekende" means "to confess". When you openly stand by a belief, add "sig til" (yourself to): "Hun bekender sig til sine værdier" (She stands by her values).

sentence.da: Hun vil **bekende**, at hun har taget pengene.
sentence.en: She will confess that she has taken the money.

at bekræfte.explanation: "At bekræfte" means "to confirm". When a result shows that a guess was right, say "Testen bekræfter vores mistanke" (The test confirms our suspicion).

sentence.da: Kan du **bekræfte**, at mødet er klokken ti?
sentence.en: Can you confirm that the meeting is at ten o'clock?

at bekymre sig.explanation: "At bekymre sig" means "to worry". To say who you worry about, add "om" (about): "Jeg bekymrer mig om dig" (I worry about you). When you say "you", "sig" becomes "dig": "Du bekymrer dig for meget" (You worry too much).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **bekymre sig**, fordi alt går godt.
sentence.en: She won't worry because everything is going well.

at bekæmpe.explanation: "At bekæmpe" means "to fight or combat". It is built from "at kæmpe" (to struggle). When you work against a harmful thing, say "Vi bekæmper fattigdom" (We fight poverty). Do not mix it up with "at slås" (to brawl): "Drengene slås i skolegården" (The boys are brawling in the schoolyard).

sentence.da: Lægerne kan **bekæmpe** sygdommen med den nye medicin.
sentence.en: The doctors can fight the disease with the new medicine.

at belaste.explanation: "At belaste" means "to burden or strain". It is built from "en last" (a load). When something harms a thing, say "Kørsel belaster miljøet" (Driving burdens the environment). When you put your problems on a person, say "Jeg vil ikke belaste dig med mine problemer" (I do not want to burden you with my problems).

sentence.da: Tunge lastbiler kan **belaste** en gammel bro for meget.
sentence.en: Heavy trucks can strain an old bridge too much.

at belyse.explanation: "At belyse" means "to shed light on". It is built from "lys" (light). Literally, it means "to light up". When a lamp lights a place, say "Projektøren belyser scenen" (The spotlight lights up the stage).

sentence.da: Rapporten skal **belyse** problemet med flere tal.
sentence.en: The report must shed light on the problem with more figures.

at belære.explanation: "At belære" means "to lecture (someone)". To say what you lecture someone about, add "om" (about): "Han belærer mig om penge" (He lectures me about money). To tell someone to stop, say "Du skal ikke belære mig" (Do not lecture me).

sentence.da: Han elsker at **belære** andre, men lytter sjældent selv.
sentence.en: He loves to lecture others but rarely listens himself.

at belønne.explanation: "At belønne" means "to reward". It is built from "en løn" (a wage). To say what the reward is for, add "for" (for): "Hun blev belønnet for sin indsats" (She was rewarded for her effort).

sentence.da: Chefen vil **belønne** de ansatte med en bonus.
sentence.en: The boss will reward the employees with a bonus.

at bemærke.explanation: "At bemærke" means "to notice or remark". When you say something in passing, it means "to remark": "Hun bemærkede, at det var koldt" (She remarked that it was cold). To make people pay attention, say "Bemærk!" (Note!)

sentence.da: Du vil **bemærke** en stor forskel med det samme.
sentence.en: You will notice a big difference right away.

at benytte.explanation: "At benytte" means "to use". It is built from "nytte" (use). When you take advantage of something, add "sig af" (yourself of): "Jeg benytter mig af tilbuddet" (I am taking advantage of the offer).

sentence.da: Gæster kan **benytte** hotellets pool hele dagen.
sentence.en: Guests can use the hotel's pool all day.

at benægte.explanation: "At benægte" means "to deny". When you reject an accusation, say "Han benægter anklagen" (He denies the accusation). Do not mix it up with "at nægte" (to refuse): "De nægter ham adgang" (They refuse him entry).

sentence.da: Hun vil **benægte**, at hun har sagt det.
sentence.en: She will deny that she said it.

at beordre.explanation: "At beordre" means "to order (command)". When someone with authority sends people somewhere, say "Chefen beordrede os hjem" (The boss ordered us home). When you order food, use "at bestille" (to order): "Vi bestiller to pizzaer" (We order two pizzas).

sentence.da: Generalen kan **beordre** soldaterne til at blive.
sentence.en: The general can order the soldiers to stay.

at beregne.explanation: "At beregne" means "to calculate". It is built from "at regne" (to do sums). To say how a price is worked out, say "Prisen beregnes ud fra vægten" (The price is calculated from the weight).

sentence.da: Computeren kan **beregne** afstanden mellem byerne på et sekund.
sentence.en: The computer can calculate the distance between the cities in a second.

at berette.explanation: "At berette" means "to report or tell". It is the verb for "en beretning" (an account): "Vi læste hans beretning om krigen" (We read his account of the war).

sentence.da: Vidnet vil **berette** om ulykken i retten i morgen.
sentence.en: The witness will report on the accident in court tomorrow.

at berige.explanation: "At berige" means "to enrich". It is built from "rig" (rich). When something brings money to a country, say "Olien har beriget landet" (The oil has enriched the country).

sentence.da: Nye venner kan **berige** dit liv mere end penge.
sentence.en: New friends can enrich your life more than money.

at berolige.explanation: "At berolige" means "to calm or reassure". It is built from "rolig" (calm). When news puts your mind at rest, say "Det beroliger mig" (That reassures me). When a doctor gives a drug that calms, the drug is "et beroligende middel" (a sedative).

sentence.da: Moren kan **berolige** barnet, når det græder.
sentence.en: The mother can calm the child when it cries.

at berøre.explanation: "At berøre" means "to touch or affect". When a matter involves many people, say "Sagen berører mange" (The matter affects many people). When something moves you emotionally, say "Jeg blev dybt berørt" (I was deeply moved).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **berøre** maleriet på museet.
sentence.en: You must not touch the painting at the museum.

at besejre.explanation: "At besejre" means "to defeat". It is built from "en sejr" (a victory). When you overcome a fear, say "Hun besejrede sin angst" (She overcame her fear).

sentence.da: Holdet vil **besejre** de regerende mestre i finalen.
sentence.en: The team will defeat the reigning champions in the final.

at besidde.explanation: "At besidde" means "to possess". When someone owns something valuable, say "Hun besidder en stor formue" (She possesses a large fortune). Do not mix it up with "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en cykel" (I have a bike).

sentence.da: En god leder skal **besidde** mod og tålmodighed.
sentence.en: A good leader must possess courage and patience.

at beskadige.explanation: "At beskadige" means "to damage". It is built from "en skade" (damage). When you describe something that is already damaged, use "beskadiget" (damaged): "en beskadiget bil" (a damaged car).

sentence.da: Stormen kan **beskadige** taget på det gamle hus.
sentence.en: The storm can damage the roof of the old house.

at beskatte.explanation: "At beskatte" means "to tax". It is built from "en skat" (a tax). The same word "skat" also means "treasure": "De fandt en skat" (They found a treasure).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **beskatte** de rigeste mere end i dag.
sentence.en: The government wants to tax the richest more than today.

at beskrive.explanation: "At beskrive" means "to describe". It is built from "at skrive" (to write), but it does not need paper. To say what you describe something as, add "som" (as): "Han beskriver hende som venlig" (He describes her as friendly).

sentence.da: Kan du **beskrive** manden for politiet?
sentence.en: Can you describe the man for the police?

at beskylde.explanation: "At beskylde" means "to accuse". It is built from "en skyld" (guilt). To name the charge, add "for" (of): "Hun blev beskyldt for at lyve" (She was accused of lying).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **beskylde** ham for tyveri uden beviser.
sentence.en: You cannot accuse him of theft without proof.

at beskytte.explanation: "At beskytte" means "to protect". When people protect themselves, add "sig" (themselves): "Cyklister beskytter sig med en hjelm" (Cyclists protect themselves with a helmet).

sentence.da: Du skal **beskytte** huden mod solen.
sentence.en: You need to protect your skin from the sun.

at beskæftige sig med.explanation: "At beskæftige sig med" means "to deal with or work with". When you ask someone what they do, say "Hvad beskæftiger du dig med?" (What do you do?) Without "sig" and "med", "at beskæftige" means "to employ": "Firmaet beskæftiger 50 personer" (The company employs 50 people).

forms.en: I have dealt with / worked with

sentence.da: Min bror vil **beskæftige sig med** klimaforskning i fremtiden.
sentence.en: My brother wants to work with climate research in the future.

at beslaglægge.explanation: "At beslaglægge" means "to confiscate". When the police take away a car, say "Politiet beslaglagde bilen" (The police seized the car).

sentence.da: Tolden kan **beslaglægge** ulovlige varer i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Customs can confiscate illegal goods at the airport.

at beslutte.explanation: "At beslutte" means "to decide". To name what you decided to do, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Vi besluttede at blive hjemme" (We decided to stay home). With "mig" (myself) it means "to make up your mind": "Jeg har besluttet mig" (I have made up my mind).

sentence.da: Vi skal **beslutte**, hvor vi vil spise i aften.
sentence.en: We have to decide where we want to eat tonight.

at beslutte sig.explanation: "At beslutte sig" means "to decide". To name the choice you made, add "for" (for) after "sig" (oneself): "Jeg besluttede mig for at blive" (I decided to stay). Without "sig", "at beslutte" is followed by "at" (to) and a verb: "Vi besluttede at flytte" (We decided to move).

sentence.da: Hun skal **beslutte sig** inden i morgen.
sentence.en: She has to decide before tomorrow.

at bestemme.explanation: "At bestemme" means "to decide". When you ask who is in charge, say "Hvem bestemmer her?" (Who is in charge here?) To say who has control over someone, add "over" (over): "Du bestemmer ikke over mig" (You do not tell me what to do).

sentence.da: Du må **bestemme**, hvad vi skal spise.
sentence.en: You get to decide what we eat.

at bestemme sig.explanation: "At bestemme sig" means "to make up one's mind". To tell someone to choose now, say "Bestem dig!" (Make up your mind!) Without "sig", "at bestemme" is for the person in charge: "Chefen bestemmer" (The boss decides).

forms.en: I have made up my mind

sentence.da: Han skal **bestemme sig** i dag.
sentence.en: He has to make up his mind today.

at bestige.explanation: "At bestige" means "to climb (a mountain)". When a king or queen takes the throne, it means "to ascend": "Hun bestiger tronen" (She ascends the throne). For a tree, use "at klatre" (to climb): "Drengen klatrer i et træ" (The boy climbs a tree).

sentence.da: Vi vil **bestige** bjerget og se solopgangen fra toppen.
sentence.en: We will climb the mountain and watch the sunrise from the top.

at bestille.explanation: "At bestille" means "to order". When you reserve a table, it means "to book": "Vi har bestilt et bord til otte" (We have booked a table for eight).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille** en pizza.
sentence.en: I would like to order a pizza.

at bestille tid.explanation: "At bestille tid" means "to make an appointment". Literally, it means "to book time": "at bestille" (to book) and "tid" (time). To name the person you will see, add "hos" (at, with): "Hun bestiller tid hos tandlægen" (She makes an appointment with the dentist).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille tid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: I would like to make an appointment with the doctor.

at bestride.explanation: "At bestride" means "to dispute". When a company or a person covers the costs, it means "to cover": "Firmaet bestrider udgifterne" (The company covers the costs).

sentence.da: Hun vil **bestride** anklagen, fordi den ikke er sand.
sentence.en: She will dispute the charge because it is not true.

at bestræbe sig.explanation: "At bestræbe sig" means "to strive". It is built from "at stræbe" (to aspire). To say what you strive to do, add "på at" (to) before the verb. When you say "we", "sig" becomes "os": "Vi bestræber os på at svare hurtigt" (We strive to answer quickly).

sentence.da: Man skal **bestræbe sig** på at være ærlig.
sentence.en: One must strive to be honest.

at bestå.explanation: "At bestå" means "to pass (an exam) or consist". When you say what something is made of, add "af" (of): "Holdet består af ti spillere" (The team consists of ten players).

sentence.da: Hun skal læse meget for at **bestå** eksamen.
sentence.en: She has to study a lot to pass the exam.

at besvare.explanation: "At besvare" means "to answer". It is built from "at svare" (to answer). "At svare" needs "på" (on): "Han svarer på brevet" (He answers the letter). "At besvare" takes no "på": "Han besvarer brevet" (He answers the letter).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **besvare** alle spørgsmålene i prøven.
sentence.en: The students must answer all the questions in the test.

at besvime.explanation: "At besvime" means "to faint". To say someone has fainted, use "er" (is), not "har" (has): "Hun er besvimet" (She has fainted).

sentence.da: I stærk varme kan man **besvime**, når man ikke drikker nok.
sentence.en: In strong heat you can faint when you do not drink enough.

at besøge.explanation: "At besøge" means "to visit". To ask whether you can come for a visit, use "at komme på besøg" (to come for a visit): "Må jeg komme på besøg?" (May I come for a visit?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **besøge** min mormor i dag.
sentence.en: I want to visit my grandmother today.

at betale.explanation: "At betale" means "to pay". When you pay a bill, no small word follows: "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill). To pay someone back, add "tilbage" (back): "Jeg betaler dig tilbage i morgen" (I will pay you back tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **betale** 40 kroner for kaffen.
sentence.en: I have to pay 40 kroner for the coffee.

at betale af.explanation: "At betale af" means "to pay off". It is built from "at betale" (to pay) and "af" (off). To ask how much someone pays toward a loan each month, say "Hvor meget betaler du af hver måned?" (How much do you pay off each month?)

sentence.da: Vi kan **betale af** på lånet hver måned.
sentence.en: We can pay down the loan every month.

at betale for.explanation: "At betale for" means "to pay for". To cover another person's share, put the person after "for": "Jeg betaler for dig" (I am paying for you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale for** kaffen.
sentence.en: I would like to pay for the coffee.

at betale med kort.explanation: "At betale med kort" means "to pay by card". To ask a shop whether you can pay by card, say "Kan jeg betale med kort?" (Can I pay by card?) To pay in cash, say "at betale kontant" (to pay in cash): "Jeg betaler kontant" (I pay in cash).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale med kort**.
sentence.en: I would like to pay by card.

at betale sig.explanation: "At betale sig" means "to pay off (be worth it)". To say what is worth doing, use "det" (it) and add "at" and a verb: "Det betaler sig at lære dansk" (It pays off to learn Danish). Do not mix it up with "at betale" (to pay money): "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill).

forms.en: it has paid off (be worth it)

sentence.da: Gode sko er dyre, men det kan **betale sig**.
sentence.en: Good shoes are expensive, but it can pay off.

at betale tilbage.explanation: "At betale tilbage" means "to pay back". When you say what money you pay back, put it before "tilbage": "Jeg betaler pengene tilbage" (I pay the money back). To name the person who gets the money, put the person straight after "betale": "Jeg betaler dig tilbage" (I pay you back).

sentence.da: Jeg har lånt penge og skal **betale tilbage**.
sentence.en: I borrowed money and have to pay back.

at betegne.explanation: "At betegne" means "to denote or describe". When you say what a word stands for, say "Ordet 'bil' betegner et køretøj" (The word 'bil' stands for a vehicle).

sentence.da: Man kan **betegne** en ugle som en natfugl.
sentence.en: You can describe an owl as a night bird.

at betjene.explanation: "At betjene" means "to serve or operate". When someone works a machine, say "Han betjener kranen" (He operates the crane). When a waiter brings food to a table, use "at servere" (to serve): "Tjeneren serverer maden" (The waiter serves the food).

sentence.da: Hun skal **betjene** kunderne ved disken, når de kommer.
sentence.en: She has to serve the customers at the counter when they come.

at betragte.explanation: "At betragte" means "to regard or consider". When you look at something calmly for a while, it means "to watch": "Hun betragter solnedgangen" (She watches the sunset).

sentence.da: Mange vil **betragte** ham som landets bedste forfatter.
sentence.en: Many regard him as the country's best author.

at betro.explanation: "At betro" means "to confide". To confide in someone, add "sig" (yourself) and "til" (to): "Hun betroede sig til sin søster" (She confided in her sister). When you hand something important to a person you trust, it means "to entrust": "Jeg betror ham nøglerne" (I entrust him with the keys).

sentence.da: Man kan **betro** sine hemmeligheder til en god ven.
sentence.en: You can confide your secrets to a good friend.

at betvivle.explanation: "At betvivle" means "to question or doubt". It is built from "at tvivle" (to doubt). No small word follows it: "Jeg betvivler hans ord" (I doubt his word). "At tvivle" needs "på" (on) instead: "Jeg tvivler på hans ord" (I doubt his word).

sentence.da: Ingen kan **betvivle**, at hun har arbejdet hårdt.
sentence.en: No one can doubt that she has worked hard.

at betyde.explanation: "At betyde" means "to mean". When something is important to you, say "Det betyder meget for mig" (It means a lot to me). When you explain what follows from something, say "Det betyder, at vi må vente" (That means that we must wait).

sentence.da: Hvad kan det ord **betyde**?
sentence.en: What can that word mean?

at beundre.explanation: "At beundre" means "to admire". When you look at something beautiful with delight, say "Vi beundrer udsigten" (We admire the view). Do not mix it up with "at kunne lide" (to like): "Jeg kan lide min nabo" (I like my neighbor).

sentence.da: Jeg kan kun **beundre** hende, fordi hun aldrig giver op.
sentence.en: I can only admire her because she never gives up.

at bevare.explanation: "At bevare" means "to preserve or keep". To say you stay calm, use "at bevare roen" (to keep calm): "Han bevarer roen" (He keeps calm). To keep a thing you own, use "at beholde" (to keep): "Jeg beholder bogen" (I keep the book).

sentence.da: Museet skal **bevare** gamle ting, så de ikke går tabt.
sentence.en: The museum has to preserve old things so they are not lost.

at bevilge.explanation: "At bevilge" means "to grant". To say that money has been granted, say "Der er bevilget to millioner kroner" (Two million kroner have been granted).

sentence.da: Politikerne vil **bevilge** flere penge til skolerne.
sentence.en: The politicians want to grant more money to the schools.

at bevise.explanation: "At bevise" means "to prove". When you show that something is true, say "Hun beviste, at det var sandt" (She proved that it was true). When you show what you can do, use "at bevise sit værd" (to prove your worth): "Han ville bevise sit værd" (He wanted to prove his worth).

sentence.da: Man kan **bevise** en teori med forsøg og målinger.
sentence.en: You can prove a theory with experiments and measurements.

at bevæge.explanation: "At bevæge" means "to move". To move yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To move house, use "at flytte" (to move): "Vi flytter til Odense" (We are moving to Odense).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **bevæge** min venstre arm.
sentence.en: I cannot move my left arm.

at bevæge sig.explanation: "At bevæge sig" means "to move". When you move your own body, say "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To carry a thing to another place, use "at flytte" (to move): "Jeg flytter bordet" (I am moving the table).

sentence.da: Katten kan ikke **bevæge sig**, fordi den sidder fast.
sentence.en: The cat cannot move because it is stuck.

at bide.explanation: "At bide" means "to bite". When an insect bites you, say "Myggen bed mig" (The mosquito bit me). To bite into food, add "i" (in): "Hun bider i æblet" (She bites into the apple). Do not mix it up with "at bede" (to ask / pray), which is spelled almost the same: "Jeg beder om hjælp" (I ask for help).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **bide** med sine skarpe tænder.
sentence.en: The dog can bite with its sharp teeth.

at bidrage.explanation: "At bidrage" means "to contribute". To say what you give to, add "til" (to): "Hun bidrager til forskningen" (She contributes to the research).

sentence.da: Alle i klassen kan **bidrage** med lidt mad.
sentence.en: Everyone in the class can contribute some food.

at binde.explanation: "At binde" means "to tie or bind". When you tie hair up, add "op" (up): "Jeg binder håret op" (I tie my hair up).

sentence.da: Vi skal **binde** hunden til træet.
sentence.en: We have to tie the dog to the tree.

at binde snørebånd.explanation: "At binde snørebånd" means "to tie shoelaces". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "snørebånd" (shoelaces). To tie a scarf, use the same verb: "Jeg binder et tørklæde" (I tie a scarf).

sentence.da: Min lille datter kan allerede **binde snørebånd**.
sentence.en: My little daughter can already tie shoelaces.

at bistå.explanation: "At bistå" means "to assist". It is the verb for "en bistand" (assistance). To name the person you help, put the person after the verb: "Revisoren bistår firmaet" (The accountant assists the company).

sentence.da: En advokat kan **bistå** dig, når du går i retten.
sentence.en: A lawyer can assist you when you go to court.

at blaffe.explanation: "At blaffe" means "to hitchhike". To ask for a ride, say "Må jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?)

sentence.da: Vi har ingen bil, men vi vil **blaffe** til kysten.
sentence.en: We have no car, but we want to hitchhike to the coast.

at blande.explanation: "At blande" means "to mix". To mix two things together, add "med" (with): "Han blander mælk med kaffe" (He mixes milk with coffee). Do not mix it up with "at blande sig" (to interfere): "Bland dig ikke i det" (Stay out of it).

sentence.da: Du skal **blande** mel og æg i en skål.
sentence.en: You have to mix flour and eggs in a bowl.

at blande sig.explanation: "At blande sig" means "to interfere". To say what you interfere in, add "i" (in): "Du skal ikke blande dig i andres liv" (You should not interfere in other people's lives). Without "sig" (yourself), "at blande" means "to mix": "Jeg blander saft og vand" (I mix cordial and water).

sentence.da: Han skal ikke **blande sig** i det.
sentence.en: He should not interfere in that.

at blegne.explanation: "At blegne" means "to fade". It is built from "bleg" (pale). When a face turns white, it means "to go pale": "Hun blegnede af skræk" (She went pale with fear).

sentence.da: Gardinerne kan **blegne**, når solen skinner på dem hver dag.
sentence.en: The curtains can fade when the sun shines on them every day.

at blinke.explanation: "At blinke" means "to blink or wink". When stars or lights shine on and off, say "Stjernerne blinker" (The stars are twinkling). When a driver signals a turn, say "Han blinker til venstre" (He signals left).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **blinke** med det ene øje.
sentence.en: I cannot wink with one eye.

at blive.explanation: "At blive" means "to become or stay". When something changes, say "Det bliver koldt i aften" (It will get cold tonight). When you do not leave, say "Jeg bliver hjemme" (I stay at home). When you say what will happen, say "Det bliver godt" (It will be good). Do not mix it up with "at være" (to be): "Han er læge" (He is a doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **blive** læge.
sentence.en: I want to become a doctor.

at blive bange.explanation: "At blive bange" means "to get scared". When you name what scares you, add "for" (of): "Han blev bange for hunden" (He got scared of the dog). Do not mix it up with "at være bange" (to be scared), which says you are scared right now: "Jeg er bange for hunde" (I am scared of dogs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive bange**, når det tordner.
sentence.en: I can get scared when it thunders.

at blive enige.explanation: "At blive enige" means "to agree". When you name what you agree on, add "om" (on): "Vi blev enige om at tage toget" (We agreed to take the train). When one person says they share an opinion, use "at være enig" (to agree) instead: "Jeg er enig" (I agree).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive enige** om en pris.
sentence.en: We have to agree on a price.

at blive forelsket.explanation: "At blive forelsket" means "to fall in love". When you name the person, use "i" (in): "Hun blev forelsket i sin kollega" (She fell in love with her coworker). When you say you are in love right now, use "at være forelsket" (to be in love): "Jeg er forelsket" (I am in love).

sentence.da: Jeg er ved at **blive forelsket** i hende.
sentence.en: I am falling in love with her.

at blive færdig.explanation: "At blive færdig" means "to finish or graduate". When you finish a task, add "med" (with) and the task: "Jeg blev færdig med lektierne" (I finished the homework). When you graduate in a profession, add "som" (as): "Hun bliver færdig som læge" (She is graduating as a doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive færdig** før frokost.
sentence.en: I would like to be done before lunch.

at blive gammel.explanation: "At blive gammel" means "to grow old". The verb "blive" (to become) also goes with other adjectives. When you say something gets cold, use "at blive kold" (to get cold). When you say something gets big, use "at blive stor" (to grow big).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive gammel** og rask.
sentence.en: I would like to grow old and stay healthy.

at blive gift.explanation: "At blive gift" means "to get married". When you name the person you marry, use "med" (with): "at blive gift med ham" (to marry him). When you say you are married right now, use "at være gift" (to be married): "Jeg er gift" (I am married).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive gift** i sommer.
sentence.en: We are going to get married this summer.

at blive glad.explanation: "At blive glad" means "to become happy". When you name what made you happy, add "for" (about): "Jeg blev glad for kagen" (I was happy about the cake). When you say you are happy right now, use "at være glad" (to be happy): "Jeg er glad" (I am happy).

sentence.da: Hun vil **blive glad**, når hun ser gaven.
sentence.en: She will be happy when she sees the gift.

at blive hjemme.explanation: "At blive hjemme" means "to stay home". Do not mix up "hjemme" (at home) and "hjem" (home). "Hjemme" says where you are: "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home). "Hjem" says where you go: "Jeg går hjem" (I am going home). In "at blive syg" (to get sick), the verb "blive" means "to become": "Jeg blev syg" (I got sick).

sentence.da: Syge børn skal **blive hjemme**.
sentence.en: Sick children have to stay home.

at blive indlagt.explanation: "At blive indlagt" means "to be hospitalized". When you name the illness, add "med" (with): "Jeg blev indlagt med lungebetændelse" (I was hospitalized with pneumonia). When you name the place, add "på" (at): "Han blev indlagt på hospitalet" (He was admitted to the hospital).

sentence.da: Hvis du er meget syg, kan du **blive indlagt**.
sentence.en: If you are very sick, you can be hospitalized.

at blive optaget.explanation: "At blive optaget" means "to be admitted". When you get a place at a school or a club after applying, use it: "Hun blev optaget i klubben" (She was admitted to the club). When a sound is recorded, "optaget" means "recorded": "Samtalen blev optaget" (The conversation was recorded).

sentence.da: Hun håber at **blive optaget** på universitetet i København.
sentence.en: She hopes to be admitted to the university in Copenhagen.

at blive overrasket.explanation: "At blive overrasket" means "to be surprised". To name the cause of the surprise, add "over" (by): "Hun blev overrasket over nyheden" (She was surprised by the news).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive overrasket** på min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I would like to be surprised on my birthday.

at blive rask.explanation: "At blive rask" means "to get better", as in recovering from an illness. When you say someone is well again, use "rask" (well): "Hun er rask igen" (She is well again). When you wish someone who is ill a quick recovery, say "God bedring!" (Get well soon!)

sentence.da: Du vil snart **blive rask**.
sentence.en: You will soon get better.

at blive skilt.explanation: "At blive skilt" means "to get divorced". When you name the person you divorce, add "fra" (from): "Hun blev skilt fra sin mand" (She got divorced from her husband). When you describe a person's current status, use "fraskilt" (divorced): "Han er fraskilt" (He is divorced).

sentence.da: Mine forældre skal **blive skilt** næste år.
sentence.en: My parents are going to get divorced next year.

at blive syg.explanation: "At blive syg" means "to get sick". When you say you are sick right now, use "at være syg" (to be sick): "Hun er syg" (She is sick).

sentence.da: Uden søvn kan man **blive syg**.
sentence.en: Without sleep you can get sick.

at blive til.explanation: "At blive til" means "to become or turn into". When one thing changes into another, put "til" (into) before the new thing: "Larven blev til en sommerfugl" (The caterpillar turned into a butterfly). When you say how someone feels, leave out "til": "Han blev træt" (He got tired).

sentence.da: Vand kan **blive til** is.
sentence.en: Water can turn into ice.

at blive træt.explanation: "At blive træt" means "to get tired". When you say you are tired right now, use "at være træt" (to be tired): "Jeg er træt" (I am tired).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive træt** af at løbe.
sentence.en: I can get tired from running.

at blive udskrevet.explanation: "At blive udskrevet" means "to be discharged", as in leaving the hospital. It is built from "ud" (out) and "at skrive" (to write). When a doctor writes out a prescription, the verb "at udskrive" is used: "Lægen udskrev en recept" (The doctor wrote out a prescription).

sentence.da: Efter en uge kan du **blive udskrevet** og tage hjem.
sentence.en: After a week you can be discharged and go home.

at blive uvenner.explanation: "At blive uvenner" means "to fall out", as in stopping being friends. It is built from "u-" (not) and "venner" (friends). When you name the other person, add "med" (with): "Jeg blev uvenner med min nabo" (I fell out with my neighbor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **blive uvenner** med dig over penge.
sentence.en: I do not want to fall out with you over money.

at blive venner.explanation: "At blive venner" means "to become friends". It always uses "venner" (friends), never "ven" (friend), because two or more people are involved: "Maria og jeg blev venner" (Maria and I became friends).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, vi kan **blive venner**.
sentence.en: I think we can become friends.

at blive vred.explanation: "At blive vred" means "to get angry". When you name the person you are angry at, add "på" (at): "Jeg blev vred på min bror" (I got angry at my brother). When you say you are angry right now, use "at være vred" (to be angry): "Han er vred" (He is angry).

sentence.da: Han kan **blive vred**, hvis jeg kommer for sent.
sentence.en: He can get angry if I am late.

at blive væk.explanation: "At blive væk" means "to stay away or go missing". When someone does not come to an event, add "fra" (from): "Han blev væk fra mødet" (He stayed away from the meeting). When you cannot find an object, use the verb about the object: "Min nøgle er blevet væk" (My key has gone missing).

forms.en: I have stayed away / gone missing

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **blive væk** fra festen.
sentence.en: I do not want to stay away from the party.

at blokere.explanation: "At blokere" means "to block". When you stop a phone number from reaching you, use the same verb: "Jeg har blokeret hans nummer" (I have blocked his number).

sentence.da: En væltet lastbil kan **blokere** hele motorvejen.
sentence.en: A tipped-over truck can block the whole highway.

at blomstre.explanation: "At blomstre" means "to bloom". It is built from "blomst" (flower). When you say a town or a business is doing well, the same verb means "to thrive": "Byen blomstrer" (The town is thriving).

sentence.da: Roserne vil **blomstre** i juni.
sentence.en: The roses will bloom in June.

at blotlægge.explanation: "At blotlægge" means "to expose". It is built from "blot" (bare) and "at lægge" (to lay), so literally it is "to lay bare". When something physical becomes visible, use it: "Regnen blotlagde rødderne" (The rain exposed the roots).

sentence.da: Undersøgelsen vil **blotlægge** fejl i systemet.
sentence.en: The investigation will expose errors in the system.

at bluffe.explanation: "At bluffe" means "to bluff". When someone pretends to know something outside a game, use the same verb: "Han bluffer, når han siger, at han kan fransk" (He is bluffing when he says he knows French).

sentence.da: Man skal kunne **bluffe**, hvis man vil vinde i poker.
sentence.en: You have to be able to bluff if you want to win at poker.

at blæse.explanation: "At blæse" means "to blow". When you blow with your mouth, name what you blow: "Jeg blæser lysene ud" (I blow the candles out). When you do not care about something, use "på" (on): "Det blæser jeg på" (I do not care about that).

sentence.da: Det kan **blæse** meget på stranden.
sentence.en: It can blow a lot on the beach.

at bløde.explanation: "At bløde" means "to bleed". To name the body part the blood comes from, add "fra" (from): "Hun blødte fra næsen" (Her nose was bleeding).

sentence.da: Han faldt og begyndte at **bløde**.
sentence.en: He fell and began to bleed.

at bo.explanation: "At bo" means "to live (somewhere)". When you say where you live, add "i" (in) and the place: "Jeg bor i Aarhus" (I live in Aarhus). Do not mix it up with "at leve" (to be alive): "Min farmor lever stadig" (My grandmother is still alive).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bo** tæt på skolen.
sentence.en: I want to live close to the school.

at bo sammen.explanation: "At bo sammen" means "to live together". When you name who you live with, add "med" (with): "Jeg bor sammen med min bror" (I live together with my brother). Without "sammen" (together), "at bo" (to live somewhere) only says where you live: "Jeg bor i Aarhus" (I live in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bo sammen** i en lille lejlighed.
sentence.en: We would like to live together in a small apartment.

at bokse.explanation: "At bokse" means "to box", as a sport. The sport itself is "boksning" (boxing). When you say you do the sport as a hobby, use "at gå til" (to go to): "Jeg går til boksning" (I do boxing).

sentence.da: Min bror vil gerne **bokse** i en klub.
sentence.en: My brother would like to box at a club.

at booke.explanation: "At booke" means "to book", as in reserving. The word comes from English. When you reserve a place to sleep, name it: "Jeg har booket et hotelværelse" (I have booked a hotel room).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **booke** et bord til fredag.
sentence.en: I want to book a table for Friday.

at bore.explanation: "At bore" means "to drill". The power tool is "en boremaskine" (a drill), built from "bore" and "maskine" (machine).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **bore** et hul i væggen.
sentence.en: I have to drill a hole in the wall.

at bortføre.explanation: "At bortføre" means "to abduct". It is built from "bort" (away) and "at føre" (to lead). To say a person was abducted, use "blive bortført" (to be abducted): "Barnet blev bortført i går" (The child was abducted yesterday).

sentence.da: Forbryderne ville **bortføre** direktøren og kræve penge.
sentence.en: The criminals wanted to abduct the director and demand money.

at bremse.explanation: "At bremse" means "to slow down". When you stop a vehicle with the brakes, it means "to brake": "Han bremsede hårdt på cyklen" (He braked hard on his bike). When something holds you back, use it too: "Regnen bremser os" (The rain slows us down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bremse**, når lyset er rødt.
sentence.en: You have to brake when the light is red.

at bringe.explanation: "At bringe" means "to bring". When you carry something along with you, you can use "at tage med" (to take along): "Jeg tager kaffe med" (I am bringing coffee). In the phrase "bringe i fare" (to put in danger), name who is in danger: "Han bragte os i fare" (He put us in danger).

sentence.da: Han vil **bringe** gaven til dig i morgen.
sentence.en: He will bring the gift to you tomorrow.

at brokke sig.explanation: "At brokke sig" means "to complain or grumble". Add "over" (about) for what bothers you: "Vi brokker os over støjen" (We complain about the noise).

sentence.da: Min bror plejer at **brokke sig** over maden.
sentence.en: My brother usually grumbles about the food.

at bruge.explanation: "At bruge" means "to use". When you spend money, the same verb is used: "Jeg bruger mange penge på mad" (I spend a lot of money on food). When you spend time, it works too: "Jeg brugte to timer på lektierne" (I spent two hours on the homework).

sentence.da: Du kan **bruge** en kniv til brød.
sentence.en: You can use a knife for bread.

at bruge op.explanation: "At bruge op" means "to use up". The small word "op" (up) adds the idea of finishing, as in "at spise op" (to eat up) and "at drikke op" (to drink up). Do not mix it up with "at bruge" (to use), which does not say that nothing is left: "Jeg bruger en kniv" (I use a knife).

sentence.da: Vi må **bruge op**, hvad vi har i køleskabet.
sentence.en: We have to use up what we have in the fridge.

at bruge penge.explanation: "At bruge penge" means "to spend money". The word "penge" (money) has no article, so do not put "en" or "et" before it: "Jeg har penge" (I have money).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bruge penge** på en jakke.
sentence.en: I would like to spend money on a jacket.

at bryde.explanation: "At bryde" means "to break". When you do not keep a promise, use it: "Han brød sit løfte" (He broke his promise). When a quiet moment ends because someone speaks, use it too: "Hun brød stilheden" (She broke the silence). Do not mix up "brød" (broke) with "et brød" (a loaf of bread): "Jeg køber et brød" (I buy a loaf of bread).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **bryde** reglerne i spillet.
sentence.en: You must not break the rules of the game.

at bryde et løfte.explanation: "At bryde et løfte" means "to break a promise". When you break a rule instead, the verb stays the same: "at bryde en regel" (to break a rule). Do not mix up "et løfte" (a promise) with "at løfte" (to lift): "Jeg løfter kassen" (I lift the box).

sentence.da: Han vil aldrig **bryde et løfte**.
sentence.en: He will never break a promise.

at bryde loven.explanation: "At bryde loven" means "to break the law". When a cup or a toy breaks, use "at gå i stykker" (to break) instead: "Koppen gik i stykker" (The cup broke).

sentence.da: Det er forkert at **bryde loven**, også når ingen ser det.
sentence.en: It is wrong to break the law, even when nobody sees it.

at brække.explanation: "At brække" means "to break (a bone)". When you hurt a bone, name it: "Hun brækkede armen" (She broke her arm). With "sig" (yourself), it means "to vomit": "Han brækkede sig" (He threw up). When a glass or plate breaks, use "at gå i stykker" (to break): "Glasset gik i stykker" (The glass broke).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **brække** benet på isen.
sentence.en: Be careful, you can break your leg on the ice.

at brænde.explanation: "At brænde" means "to burn". When food stays too long in the oven or pan, use it: "Jeg brændte brødet" (I burned the bread). When you hurt your skin on something hot, use it too: "Jeg brændte min hånd" (I burned my hand).

sentence.da: Bålet kan **brænde** hele natten.
sentence.en: The campfire can burn all night.

at brænde ud.explanation: "At brænde ud" means "to burn out". When a candle burns until nothing is left, use it: "Stearinlyset brændte ud" (The candle burned out). When a person is worn out from too much work, use it too: "Han er brændt ud" (He has burned out).

sentence.da: Hvis du arbejder for meget, kan du **brænde ud**.
sentence.en: If you work too much, you can burn out.

at brøle.explanation: "At brøle" means "to roar". When people laugh very loudly, use "af" (with): "Vi brølede af grin" (We roared with laughter).

sentence.da: Løver kan **brøle** så højt, at man hører dem langt væk.
sentence.en: Lions can roar so loudly that you hear them far away.

at bukke.explanation: "At bukke" means "to bow". Do not mix it up with "at bukke sig" (to bend down): "Jeg bukker mig for at samle pennen op" (I bend down to pick up the pen).

sentence.da: I Japan plejer man at **bukke** for hinanden.
sentence.en: In Japan people usually bow to each other.

at bukke sig.explanation: "At bukke sig" means "to bend down". The word "sig" (yourself) separates it from "at bukke" (to bow): "Han bukker for publikum" (He bows to the audience). When you bend down for something, add "efter" (for): "Jeg bukker mig efter nøglen" (I bend down for the key).

sentence.da: Han kan ikke **bukke sig**, fordi han har ondt i ryggen.
sentence.en: He cannot bend down because his back hurts.

at burde.explanation: "At burde" means "ought to or should". When you say what someone ought to do, use "bør" or "burde": "Du bør hvile dig" (You ought to rest). Do not mix it up with "at skulle" (to have to): "Du skal hvile dig" (You have to rest).

related.en: to have no choice but to

sentence.da: Du **burde** sove mere, fordi du er træt.
sentence.en: You should sleep more because you are tired.

at byde.explanation: "At byde" means "to offer or bid". When you offer food or drink, add "på" (on): "Må jeg byde på en kop kaffe?" (May I offer you a cup of coffee?) When you say how much you bid, put the amount right after the verb: "Jeg byder tusind kroner" (I bid a thousand kroner).

sentence.da: På en auktion kan man **byde** på gamle møbler.
sentence.en: At an auction you can bid on old furniture.

at byde velkommen.explanation: "At byde velkommen" means "to welcome". It is built from "at byde" (to offer) and "velkommen" (welcome). To name the place, add "til" (to): "Vi byder dig velkommen til Danmark" (We welcome you to Denmark).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **byde velkommen** til de nye elever.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to welcome the new students.

at bygge.explanation: "At bygge" means "to build". When you make a structure, name it after the verb: "Han bygger en garage" (He is building a garage). When you say a story rests on facts, add "på" (on): "Filmen bygger på en sand historie" (The film is based on a true story).

sentence.da: Man kan **bygge** et hus af træ.
sentence.en: You can build a house from wood.

at bygge om.explanation: "At bygge om" means "to rebuild or convert". The small word "om" adds the idea of doing something over in a new way, as in "at lave om" (to redo) and "at flytte om" (to rearrange). When you change a building for a new use, add "til" (into): "De byggede laden om til et hus" (They converted the barn into a house).

sentence.da: Vi skal **bygge om** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We are going to remodel the kitchen.

at bygge på.explanation: "At bygge på" means "to build on or add on". When you add a new part to a building, use it: "De byggede en ny etage på" (They added a new floor). When you say a film rests on a book, it means "to be based on": "Filmen bygger på en bog" (The film is based on a book).

forms.en: I have built on / added on

sentence.da: Vi vil **bygge på** huset, fordi vi får et barn.
sentence.en: We want to add on to the house because we are having a baby.

at bytte.explanation: "At bytte" means "to exchange". When you ask someone to swap places with you, use it: "Vil du bytte plads?" (Do you want to swap seats?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bytte** skjorten til en større.
sentence.en: I want to exchange the shirt for a bigger one.

at bære.explanation: "At bære" means "to carry or wear". When you say what clothes you have on, you can use "at have på" (literally, "to have on"): "Jeg har en jakke på" (I am wearing a jacket).

sentence.da: Kan du **bære** min taske til bilen?
sentence.en: Can you carry my bag to the car?

at bøje.explanation: "At bøje" means "to bend". When you bend an object, name it: "Han bøjede grenen" (He bent the branch). When you bend your own body down, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg bøjer mig" (I bend down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bøje** knæene, når du løfter.
sentence.en: You have to bend your knees when you lift.

at børste tænder.explanation: "At børste tænder" means "to brush teeth". Danish leaves out "mine" (my), so you say just "tænder" (teeth): "Har du børstet tænder?" (Have you brushed your teeth?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal **børste tænder** hver aften.
sentence.en: I have to brush my teeth every evening.

at bøvse.explanation: "At bøvse" means "to burp". The matching noun is "en bøvs" (a burp).

sentence.da: Babyen skal **bøvse** efter maden.
sentence.en: The baby has to burp after the meal.

bacon.explanation: "Bacon" means "bacon". Do not mix it up with "skinke" (ham): "Jeg har skinke på brødet" (I have ham on the bread).

sentence.da: Jeg steger fire skiver **bacon** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I fry four slices of bacon for breakfast.

badebukser.explanation: "Badebukser" means "swim trunks". It is built from "bade" (bathing) and "bukser" (pants). It is plural, so use "mine" (my), not "min": "Jeg har glemt mine badebukser" (I forgot my swim trunks).

sentence.da: Drenge har **badebukser** på, når de svømmer.
sentence.en: Boys wear swim trunks when they swim.

badetøj.explanation: "Badetøj" means "swimwear". It is built from "bade" (bathing) and "tøj" (clothes). This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Jeg har badetøj med" (I have swimwear with me).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **badetøj** og håndklæde med til stranden.
sentence.en: I am bringing swimwear and a towel to the beach.

badminton.explanation: "Badminton" means "badminton". When you say you do the sport as a hobby, use "at gå til" (to go to): "Jeg går til badminton om tirsdagen" (I do badminton on Tuesdays).

sentence.da: Man spiller **badminton** med en ketsjer og en fjerbold.
sentence.en: You play badminton with a racket and a shuttlecock.

bag.explanation: "Bag" means "behind". It always needs a thing after it: "bag bilen" (behind the car). When you name nothing, use "bagved" (at the back) instead: "Katten sidder bagved" (The cat is sitting at the back).

sentence.da: Barnet gemmer sig **bag** træet.
sentence.en: The child hides behind the tree.

bagage.explanation: "Bagage" means "luggage". This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Min bagage er tung" (My luggage is heavy). When you talk about one specific kind of luggage, use its name: "en kuffert" (a suitcase).

sentence.da: Vi lander i lufthavnen og henter vores **bagage**.
sentence.en: We land at the airport and pick up our luggage.

bagefter.explanation: "Bagefter" means "afterwards". When you say what happens next, it stands alone: "Vi spiser, og bagefter ser vi film" (We eat, and afterwards we watch a film). When you name the thing that something follows, use "efter" (after) instead: "efter maden" (after the meal).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser nu og vasker op **bagefter**.
sentence.en: I eat now and wash the dishes afterwards.

bagepapir.explanation: "Bagepapir" means "baking paper". It is built from "bage" (to bake) and "papir" (paper).

sentence.da: Kagen sidder ikke fast, fordi jeg bruger **bagepapir**.
sentence.en: The cake does not stick, because I use baking paper.

bagepulver.explanation: "Bagepulver" means "baking powder". It is built from "bage" (to bake) and "pulver" (powder).

sentence.da: Kagen hæver ikke uden **bagepulver**.
sentence.en: The cake does not rise without baking powder.

bagfra.explanation: "Bagfra" means "from behind". It is built from "bag" (behind) and "fra" (from). When you see someone from the back, say: "Jeg så ham bagfra" (I saw him from behind). When you name the place where something is, use "bag" (behind): "bag huset" (behind the house).

sentence.da: Cyklisten blev ramt **bagfra** af en bil.
sentence.en: The cyclist was hit from behind by a car.

baglæns.explanation: "Baglæns" means "backwards". When you describe how someone moves, put it after the verb: "Han går baglæns" (He walks backwards). When you tell someone to return to where they were, use "tilbage" (back): "Gå tilbage!" (Go back!)

sentence.da: Vi tæller **baglæns** fra ti, når raketten skal starte.
sentence.en: We count backwards from ten when the rocket is about to launch.

bagom.explanation: "Bagom" means "around behind". It is built from "bag" (behind) and "om" (around). When you go to the back of a place, use it with a verb of movement: "Han cyklede bagom skolen" (He cycled around behind the school). For a spot where something simply is, use "bag" (behind): "Katten sidder bag døren" (The cat sits behind the door).

sentence.da: Vi går **bagom** huset og kommer ind gennem køkkenet.
sentence.en: We go around the back of the house and come in through the kitchen.

bagt.explanation: "Bagt" means "baked". It comes from the verb "at bage" (to bake). Do not mix it up with "stegt" (fried): "stegte æg" (fried eggs).

sentence.da: Jeg laver **bagt** laks i ovnen.
sentence.en: I make baked salmon in the oven.

bagud.explanation: "Bagud" means "be behind". When you say you are late with something, add "med" (with): "Han er bagud med huslejen" (He is behind on the rent). For where something sits, use "bag" (behind): "Hunden ligger bag sofaen" (The dog lies behind the sofa).

sentence.da: Vi ligger **bagud** med to mål, men der er tid tilbage.
sentence.en: We are behind by two goals, but there is time left.

bagved.explanation: "Bagved" means "at the back". No noun follows it: "Han står bagved" (He is standing at the back). If you name the person he is behind, use "bag" (behind): "Han står bag mig" (He is standing behind me).

forms.en: He is standing at the back.
The house is at the back.

sentence.da: Emma står **bagved** og ikke foran.
sentence.en: Emma stands at the back and not in front.

ballade.explanation: "En ballade" means "a fuss". To say someone is making a fuss, use "at lave ballade" (to make trouble): "Børnene laver ballade" (The children are making trouble).

sentence.da: Der er altid **ballade**, når børnene leger.
sentence.en: There is always a fuss when the children play.

balsam.explanation: "En balsam" means "a conditioner". When you say what you use after washing your hair, say: "Jeg bruger balsam efter hårvask" (I use conditioner after washing my hair).

sentence.da: **Balsam** gør håret blødt og let at rede.
sentence.en: Conditioner makes hair soft and easy to comb.

bange.explanation: "Bange" means "afraid". To name the thing you fear, add "for" (of): "Hun er bange for edderkopper" (She is afraid of spiders). To calm someone, say "Vær ikke bange!" (Do not be afraid!)

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **bange** i mørket.
sentence.en: I am very scared in the dark.

bange for.explanation: "Bange for" means "afraid of". When a whole sentence follows, it means "afraid that": "Jeg er bange for, at det er sandt" (I am afraid it is true).

forms.en: She is afraid of the dark.

forms.da: Er du bange for at flyve?

sentence.da: Børnene er **bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: The children are afraid of the dark.

banko.explanation: "Banko" means "bingo". When someone wins, they say the word out loud: "Hvem vandt?" "Det gjorde jeg. Banko!" (Who won? I did. Bingo!)

sentence.da: Til **banko** krydser vi tal af, når de bliver råbt op.
sentence.en: At bingo we cross off numbers when they are called out.

barberskum.explanation: "Barberskum" means "shaving foam". It is built from "at barbere" (to shave) and "skum" (foam). The same "skum" is in "et skumbad" (a bubble bath).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **barberskum**, når jeg barberer mig.
sentence.en: I use shaving foam when I shave.

bare.explanation: "Bare" means "just". When you tell someone they may go ahead, it means "go ahead": "Kom bare ind" (Come on in). When you say an amount is small, it means "only": "Jeg har bare to timer" (I only have two hours).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bare** sove i dag.
sentence.en: I just want to sleep today.

bark.explanation: "En bark" means "bark", as in the outside of a tree. Do not mix it up with the sound a dog makes, "at gø" (to bark): "Hunden begynder at gø" (The dog starts to bark).

sentence.da: Birkens **bark** er hvid og kan skrælles af i strimler.
sentence.en: The birch bark is white and can be peeled off in strips.

barmhjertighed.explanation: "Barmhjertighed" means "mercy". This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Dommeren viste barmhjertighed" (The judge showed mercy).

sentence.da: Han bad om **barmhjertighed**, men dommeren sagde nej.
sentence.en: He asked for mercy, but the judge said no.

barsel.explanation: "Barsel" means "parental leave". Both mothers and fathers can take it: "Han er på barsel" (He is on parental leave).

sentence.da: Min bror er på **barsel** og passer sin lille datter hjemme.
sentence.en: My brother is on parental leave and looks after his little daughter at home.

barsk.explanation: "Barsk" means "harsh". When you describe a person's voice, use it too: "en barsk stemme" (a harsh voice). When you describe wild nature, use it: "en barsk natur" (a harsh landscape).

sentence.da: Vinteren i Nordnorge er **barsk**, og vinden er iskold.
sentence.en: The winter in northern Norway is harsh, and the wind is ice cold.

basilikum.explanation: "Basilikum" means "basil". This word has no article: "Vi har basilikum i haven" (We have basil in the garden).

sentence.da: Vi plukker frisk **basilikum** til pizzaen.
sentence.en: We pick fresh basil for the pizza.

basketball.explanation: "Basketball" means "basketball". When you mean the ball, add "en": "Jeg har købt en basketball" (I bought a basketball).

sentence.da: Man kaster bolden i en kurv i **basketball**.
sentence.en: You throw the ball into a basket in basketball.

bedre.explanation: "Bedre" means "better". When you say you feel better after being ill, say: "Jeg har det bedre" (I feel better).

sentence.da: Din nye cykel er **bedre** end den gamle.
sentence.en: Your new bike is better than the old one.

bedre sent end aldrig.explanation: "Bedre sent end aldrig" means "better late than never". When someone arrives late, you can answer them: "Undskyld, jeg er sen." "Bedre sent end aldrig." (Sorry, I am late. Better late than never.)

forms.da: Nå, men bedre sent end aldrig.
Han kom, og det er bedre sent end aldrig.
forms.en: He came, and better late than never.

sentence.da: Du kom for sent, men **bedre sent end aldrig**.
sentence.en: You came late, but better late than never.

bedring.explanation: "En bedring" means "a recovery". When something other than health gets better, it means "an improvement": "en bedring i økonomien" (an improvement in the economy).

sentence.da: Lægen ser en langsom **bedring** efter operationen.
sentence.en: The doctor sees a slow recovery after the operation.

bedst.explanation: "Bedst" means "best". When you say what you like best, use "kan bedst lide" (like best): "Jeg kan bedst lide kaffe" (I like coffee best).

sentence.da: Carl er **bedst** i klassen.
sentence.en: Carl is the best in the class.

bedst før.explanation: "Bedst før" means "best before". Do not mix it up with "sidste anvendelsesdato" (use-by date): "Sidste anvendelsesdato er i dag" (The use-by date is today).

forms.en: best before the end of June

sentence.da: Mælken er **bedst før** fredag.
sentence.en: The milk is best before Friday.

bedsteforældre.explanation: "Bedsteforældre" means "grandparents". It is built from "bedste" (best) and "forældre" (parents).

sentence.da: Mine **bedsteforældre** er mine forældres forældre.
sentence.en: My grandparents are my parents' parents.

bedøvet.explanation: "Bedøvet" means "anesthetized". When someone is dazed after a shock, it means "stunned": "Hun var bedøvet af chok" (She was stunned by the shock).

sentence.da: Tandlægen gav mig en indsprøjtning, og nu er min mund **bedøvet**.
sentence.en: The dentist gave me an injection, and now my mouth is numb.

begavet.explanation: "Begavet" means "gifted". For a person with a talent in one skill, use "talentfuld" (talented) instead: "en talentfuld pianist" (a talented pianist).

sentence.da: Hun er **begavet** og lærte at læse som fireårig.
sentence.en: She is gifted and learned to read at four.

begge.explanation: "Begge" means "both of them". It is only for two: "Begge er her" (Both are here). When you mean any number of people, use "alle" (everyone): "Alle er her" (Everyone is here). When you add "to" (two), the meaning stays the same: "Jeg kender dem begge to" (I know both of them).

sentence.da: Mine to børn er **begge** hjemme.
sentence.en: My two children are both at home.

begrænset.explanation: "Begrænset" means "limited". When you say there is only a little room, use it before the noun: "begrænset plads" (limited space). It comes from "en grænse" (a border).

sentence.da: Vi har kun **begrænset** tid, men vi kan nå en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: We only have limited time, but we can fit in a cup of coffee.

begær.explanation: "Et begær" means "a desire". When you name what is desired, add "efter" (for): "begær efter anerkendelse" (desire for recognition).

sentence.da: Hans **begær** efter magt gjorde ham til en farlig mand.
sentence.en: His desire for power made him a dangerous man.

behagelig.explanation: "Behagelig" means "comfortable". When you describe a voice or a temperature, it means "pleasant": "en behagelig stemme" (a pleasant voice), "en behagelig temperatur" (a pleasant temperature).

sentence.da: Sofaen er blød og **behagelig**.
sentence.en: The sofa is soft and comfortable.

behjælpelig.explanation: "Behjælpelig" means "helpful". It comes from "en hjælp" (a help). When you describe someone who helped you, say: "Han var meget behjælpelig" (He was very helpful).

sentence.da: Kan du være **behjælpelig** med at finde min kuffert?
sentence.en: Could you help me find my suitcase?

beige.explanation: "Beige" means "beige". To ask about a color and answer: "Hvilken farve har huset?" "Det er beige." (Which color is the house? It is beige.)

sentence.da: Sandet på stranden er **beige**.
sentence.en: The sand on the beach is beige.

bekendt.explanation: "Bekendt" means "familiar". When you talk about a person you know only slightly, use the noun "en bekendt" (an acquaintance): "Jeg mødte en bekendt i byen" (I met an acquaintance in town). To say you know about something, use "med" (with) after it: "Jeg er bekendt med reglerne" (I am familiar with the rules).

sentence.da: Hendes stemme lyder **bekendt**.
sentence.en: Her voice sounds familiar.

bekvem.explanation: "Bekvem" means "convenient". When you talk about a seat or clothes that feel good, it also means "comfortable": "en bekvem stol" (a comfortable chair). It is built into "en bekvemmelighed" (a convenience).

sentence.da: Det er en **bekvem** måde at betale på.
sentence.en: It is a convenient way to pay.

bekymrende.explanation: "Bekymrende" means "worrying". To say the news or a sign causes worry, use "bekymrende": "Nyheden er bekymrende" (The news is worrying). To say you feel worry yourself, use the similar word "bekymret" (worried): "Jeg er bekymret" (I am worried).

sentence.da: Det er **bekymrende**, at så mange unge sover for lidt.
sentence.en: It is worrying that so many young people sleep too little.

belysning.explanation: "Belysning" means "lighting". It comes from the verb "at belyse" (to illuminate). When you talk about looking closely at a subject, it has another meaning: "en belysning af sagen" (a closer look at the matter).

sentence.da: God **belysning** i gaden gør os trygge, når det er mørkt.
sentence.en: Good lighting in the street makes us feel safe when it is dark.

bemærkelsesværdig.explanation: "Bemærkelsesværdig" means "remarkable". It is built from "at bemærke" (to notice) and "værdig" (worthy). To say that a fact deserves attention, say: "Det er bemærkelsesværdigt, at hun vandt" (It is remarkable that she won).

sentence.da: Hendes udholdenhed er **bemærkelsesværdig**, når man tænker på hendes alder.
sentence.en: Her stamina is remarkable when you think of her age.

benzin.explanation: "Benzin" means "gasoline". To say you fill the car with fuel, use the verb "at tanke" (to fill up): "Jeg skal tanke benzin" (I need to fill up with gasoline).

sentence.da: Min bil kører på **benzin**, ikke på diesel.
sentence.en: My car runs on gasoline, not on diesel.

beredvillighed.explanation: "En beredvillighed" means "a readiness", as in readiness to help. Do not mix it up with "et beredskab" (an emergency service): "Beredskabet kom hurtigt" (The emergency service came quickly).

sentence.da: Når man gerne og hurtigt hjælper, viser man **beredvillighed**.
sentence.en: When you help gladly and quickly, you show readiness.

berettiget.explanation: "Berettiget" means "justified". When you say someone has the right to receive something, it means "entitled" and takes "til" (to): "Du er berettiget til hjælp" (You are entitled to help).

sentence.da: Hendes kritik var **berettiget**, fordi fejlen var tydelig.
sentence.en: Her criticism was justified because the mistake was obvious.

beruset.explanation: "Beruset" means "intoxicated". It is the formal word, as in "en beruset bilist" (an intoxicated driver). In everyday talk, to say someone is drunk, use "fuld": "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Det er forbudt at køre bil, når man er **beruset**.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive a car when you are drunk.

berømt.explanation: "Berømt" means "famous". To say what someone or something is famous for, put "for" after it: "Den er berømt for sin ost" (It is famous for its cheese).

sentence.da: Hun er en **berømt** sanger i hele landet.
sentence.en: She is a famous singer all over the country.

beskadiget.explanation: "Beskadiget" means "damaged". It comes from the verb "at beskadige" (to damage). To say a package arrived with harm, say: "Pakken er beskadiget" (The package is damaged). To say a thing no longer works at all, use the similar word "ødelagt" (broken): "Telefonen er ødelagt" (The phone is broken).

sentence.da: Bilen er **beskadiget** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The car is damaged after the accident.

beskeden.explanation: "Beskeden" means "modest". When you talk about a small amount, it has another meaning: "en beskeden løn" (a modest salary). Do not mix it up with "en besked" (a message): "Jeg fik en besked" (I got a message).

sentence.da: Hun er **beskeden** og snakker aldrig om sine succeser.
sentence.en: She is modest and never talks about her successes.

beskidt.explanation: "Beskidt" means "dirty". To say you made something dirty, use it after "at gøre" (to make): "Jeg har gjort tøjet beskidt" (I have made the clothes dirty).

sentence.da: Man bliver **beskidt** af at lege i mudder.
sentence.en: You get dirty from playing in mud.

beskyttelse.explanation: "En beskyttelse" means "a protection". It comes from the verb "at beskytte" (to protect). The word begins many compounds, such as "beskyttelsesbriller" (safety goggles).

sentence.da: Solcreme giver **beskyttelse** mod solen.
sentence.en: Sunscreen gives protection from the sun.

beskyttende.explanation: "Beskyttende" means "protective". It comes from the verb "at beskytte" (to protect). When you talk about a person who watches over someone, use it too: "en beskyttende far" (a protective father).

sentence.da: Han bruger **beskyttende** briller, når han saver i træ.
sentence.en: He uses protective goggles when he saws wood.

beslutsomhed.explanation: "En beslutsomhed" means "a determination". Do not mix it up with "en beslutning" (a decision): "Vi tog en beslutning" (We made a decision).

sentence.da: Hun tøvede ikke, men handlede med **beslutsomhed**.
sentence.en: She did not hesitate but acted with determination.

beslægtet.explanation: "Beslægtet" means "related". To ask whether two people are in the same family, say: "Er I beslægtede?" (Are you two related?). It comes from "en slægt" (a family line).

sentence.da: Ulven er tæt **beslægtet** med vores hunde.
sentence.en: The wolf is closely related to our dogs.

bestemt.explanation: "Bestemt" means "definitely". To stress that something is certain, put it in the sentence: "Hun kommer bestemt" (She is definitely coming). To point at one particular thing, it means "certain": "en bestemt bog" (a certain book).

forms.en: I definitely do not want to

sentence.da: Det er **bestemt** en god idé.
sentence.en: That is definitely a good idea.

bestemt form.explanation: "En bestemt form" means "a definite form". It is the version of a word that says "the". Danish puts "the" on the end of the word: "en hund" (a dog) becomes "hunden" (the dog). For a word with "et", the same happens: "et hus" (a house) becomes "huset" (the house).

sentence.da: Ordet bilen er i **bestemt form**, men en bil er det ikke.
sentence.en: The word bilen is in the definite form, but en bil is not.

bestik.explanation: "Et bestik" means "a set of cutlery". To name one piece of cutlery, say "en kniv" (a knife), "en gaffel" (a fork) or "en ske" (a spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger **bestik** og tallerkener på bordet.
sentence.en: I put cutlery and plates on the table.

bestikkelse.explanation: "En bestikkelse" means "a bribe". It comes from the verb "at bestikke" (to bribe). To name the crime, leave out "en": "Han blev anklaget for bestikkelse" (He was accused of bribery).

sentence.da: Politiet mener, at manden tog imod **bestikkelse** fra firmaet.
sentence.en: The police believe the man took bribes from the company.

besvær.explanation: "Et besvær" means "a hassle". To answer someone who thanks you for your effort: "Tak for hjælpen." "Det er ikke noget besvær." (Thanks for the help. It is no trouble.)

sentence.da: Det er for meget **besvær** at rejse så langt for et møde.
sentence.en: It is too much trouble to travel so far for a meeting.

besværlig.explanation: "Besværlig" means "troublesome". It comes from "et besvær" (a hassle). When you talk about a person who is awkward to deal with, use it too: "en besværlig kunde" (a difficult customer).

sentence.da: Vejen til hytten er **besværlig**, fordi den er stejl og mudret.
sentence.en: The road to the cabin is troublesome because it is steep and muddy.

beton.explanation: "Beton" means "concrete". When you mean the material in general, leave out "en": "Der er beton overalt" (There is concrete everywhere). Do not mix it up with "cement" (cement), the powder: "Cement er et gråt pulver" (Cement is a gray powder).

sentence.da: Gulvet i kælderen er lavet af **beton**.
sentence.en: The floor in the basement is made of concrete.

betydelig.explanation: "Betydelig" means "significant". To say an amount or change is large, use "betydelig": "en betydelig stigning" (a considerable rise). To say something has great meaning, use the similar word "betydningsfuld" (meaningful): "en betydningsfuld opdagelse" (a meaningful discovery).

sentence.da: Hun har en **betydelig** indflydelse på beslutningen.
sentence.en: She has a significant influence on the decision.

betydningsfuld.explanation: "Betydningsfuld" means "significant". It is built from "betydning" (meaning) and "fuld" (full). To say a discovery matters a lot, say: "en betydningsfuld opdagelse" (a significant discovery). Do not mix it up with "betydelig" (considerable), which says an amount is large: "en betydelig stigning" (a considerable rise).

sentence.da: Opfindelsen af trykpressen var en **betydningsfuld** begivenhed i historien.
sentence.en: The invention of the printing press was a significant event in history.

betænkelig.explanation: "Betænkelig" means "worrying". To say you have doubts about a plan, add "ved" (about): "Jeg er betænkelig ved planen" (I am doubtful about the plan).

sentence.da: Situationen er **betænkelig**, fordi floden stiger hurtigt.
sentence.en: The situation is worrying because the river is rising fast.
