bevidst.explanation: "Bevidst" means "deliberate". To say someone did something on purpose, use it after the verb: "Hun gjorde det bevidst" (She did it on purpose).

sentence.da: Han er **bevidst** om, at det kan være farligt.
sentence.en: He is aware that it can be dangerous.

bevidsthed.explanation: "Bevidsthed" means "consciousness". To say someone passes out, use "at miste bevidstheden" (to lose consciousness). To say a patient is awake and aware, use "ved bevidsthed" (conscious): "Patienten er ved bevidsthed" (The patient is conscious).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken kom han til **bevidsthed** igen.
sentence.en: After the accident he regained consciousness.

bevidstløs.explanation: "Bevidstløs" means "unconscious". The ending "løs" means "without", as in "hjælpeløs" (helpless) and "håbløs" (hopeless).

sentence.da: Efter faldet lå cyklisten **bevidstløs** på vejen.
sentence.en: After the fall the cyclist lay unconscious on the road.

bevismateriale.explanation: "Et bevismateriale" means "a body of evidence". It is built from "et bevis" (a proof) and "et materiale" (a material). To say a lawyer shows it in court, use "at fremlægge" (to present): "Anklageren fremlægger bevismateriale" (The prosecutor presents evidence).

sentence.da: Fotos, breve og optagelser er alt sammen **bevismateriale** i en retssag.
sentence.en: Photos, letters and recordings are all evidence in a trial.

bevæbnet.explanation: "Bevæbnet" means "armed". To name the weapon, add "med" (with): "Vagterne er bevæbnede med pistoler" (The guards are armed with pistols).

sentence.da: Politiet sagde, at manden var **bevæbnet** med en kniv.
sentence.en: The police said that the man was armed with a knife.

beæret.explanation: "Beæret" means "honored". It comes from "en ære" (an honor). To give the reason, add "over" (about): "Jeg er beæret over invitationen" (I am honored by the invitation).

sentence.da: Hun følte sig **beæret**, da kongen takkede hende personligt.
sentence.en: She felt honored when the king thanked her personally.

bifald.explanation: "Et bifald" means "applause". When you say people approve of an idea, it also means "approval": "Forslaget fik bifald" (The proposal got approval).

sentence.da: Efter koncerten fik orkestret et langt **bifald** fra publikum.
sentence.en: After the concert, the orchestra got long applause from the audience.

billedkunst.explanation: "Billedkunst" means "art (the subject)". It is built from "et billede" (a picture) and "kunst" (art).

sentence.da: I **billedkunst** lærer børnene at tegne og male.
sentence.en: In art, the children learn to draw and paint.

billig.explanation: "Billig" means "cheap". To say something looks poorly made, use it too: "Jakken ser billig ud" (The jacket looks cheap). To ask a shop assistant for a lower price, say: "Har du noget billigere?" (Do you have something cheaper?)

sentence.da: Maden er **billig**, kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: The food is cheap, only twenty kroner.

biodiversitet.explanation: "Biodiversitet" means "biodiversity". It is built from "bio" (life) and "diversitet" (diversity). To say you look after it, use "at beskytte" (to protect): "Vi skal beskytte biodiversiteten" (We must protect biodiversity).

sentence.da: Skoven har stor **biodiversitet**, fordi der lever mange forskellige arter.
sentence.en: The forest has great biodiversity because many different species live there.

biologi.explanation: "Biologi" means "biology". It is built from "bio" (life) and "logi" (study). To say you are good at it, use "til" (at): "Jeg er god til biologi" (I am good at biology).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om dyr og planter i **biologi**.
sentence.en: We learn about animals and plants in biology.

biologisk.explanation: "Biologisk" means "biological". It comes from "biologi" (biology). To say something rots away naturally, use "biologisk nedbrydeligt" (biodegradable): "Posen er biologisk nedbrydelig" (The bag is biodegradable).

sentence.da: **Biologisk** affald er rester af planter og dyr.
sentence.en: Biological waste is what is left of plants and animals.

bitter.explanation: "Bitter" means "bitter". When you describe a person who stays angry about something that happened, use it too: "Hun er bitter" (She is bitter).

sentence.da: Kaffen er for **bitter** for mig.
sentence.en: The coffee is too bitter for me.

blandet.explanation: "Blandet" means "mixed". To say a dish has several kinds in it, use "blandet": "en blandet salat" (a mixed salad). To describe a feeling that is both good and bad, use the plural: "blandede følelser" (mixed feelings).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **blandet** slik til børnene.
sentence.en: I buy mixed candy for the kids.

blandt.explanation: "Blandt" means "among". To say someone is one of a group, say: "Han er blandt de bedste" (He is among the best). To talk about exactly two things, use "mellem" (between) instead: "mellem huset og træet" (between the house and the tree).

sentence.da: Katten gemmer sig **blandt** blomsterne.
sentence.en: The cat hides among the flowers.

blandt andet.explanation: "Blandt andet" means "among other things". It is built from "blandt" (among) and "andet" (other things). In writing it is shortened to "bl.a.": "Hun taler bl.a. fransk" (She speaks French, among other things).

forms.da: Vi talte blandt andet om musik.
forms.en: We talked about music, among other things.
She can swim, among other things.

sentence.da: Jeg købte **blandt andet** brød og ost.
sentence.en: I bought bread and cheese, among other things.

blank.explanation: "Blank" means "shiny". When you talk about a page with nothing on it, it means "blank": "et blankt ark" (a blank sheet).

sentence.da: Bilen er **blank**, fordi jeg har vasket den.
sentence.en: The car is shiny because I washed it.

bleg.explanation: "Bleg" means "pale". When you talk about colors that look washed out, use it too: "blege farver" (pale colors).

sentence.da: Hun blev helt **bleg** i ansigtet, da hun hørte nyheden.
sentence.en: She turned completely pale in the face when she heard the news.

blind.explanation: "Blind" means "blind". When you say someone does not notice something, add "for" (to): "Han er blind for sine fejl" (He is blind to his faults).

sentence.da: Han er **blind** og kan ikke se.
sentence.en: He is blind and cannot see.

blod.explanation: "Blod" means "blood". It is the first part of many longer words: "blodprøve" (blood test) and "blodtryk" (blood pressure).

sentence.da: Lægen tager en prøve af mit **blod**.
sentence.en: The doctor takes a sample of my blood.

blodig.explanation: "Blodig" means "bloody". It comes from "blod" (blood). In the phrase "blodig alvor" it means "deadly serious": "Det er blodig alvor" (It is deadly serious).

sentence.da: Han fik en **blodig** næse, da bolden ramte ham.
sentence.en: He got a bloody nose when the ball hit him.

blodsukker.explanation: "Et blodsukker" means "a blood sugar". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "sukker" (sugar). To say you check it, use "at måle" (to measure): "Jeg skal måle mit blodsukker" (I need to measure my blood sugar).

sentence.da: Efter et stort måltid stiger mit **blodsukker**.
sentence.en: After a big meal my blood sugar rises.

blodtryk.explanation: "Et blodtryk" means "blood pressure". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "tryk" (pressure). To say yours is too high, say: "Jeg har for højt blodtryk" (My blood pressure is too high).

sentence.da: Lægen måler mit **blodtryk** med en manchet om overarmen.
sentence.en: The doctor measures my blood pressure with a cuff around the upper arm.

blokeret.explanation: "Blokeret" means "blocked". When you talk about a bank card or account that has been stopped, use it too: "Dit kort er blokeret" (Your card is blocked).

sentence.da: Vejen er **blokeret** af et væltet træ.
sentence.en: The road is blocked by a fallen tree.

blomkål.explanation: "En blomkål" means "a cauliflower". It is built from "blomst" (flower) and "kål" (cabbage), so it literally means "flower cabbage".

sentence.da: **Blomkål** er hvid og ligner en lille blomst.
sentence.en: Cauliflower is white and looks like a small flower.

blond.explanation: "Blond" means "blond". To ask about and describe someone's hair: "Hvad farve har hendes hår?" "Det er blondt." (What color is her hair? It is blond.)

sentence.da: Min søster er **blond**, men jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is blond, but I have dark hair.

blot.explanation: "Blot" means "just". To express a wish, it means "only": "Havde jeg blot vidst det!" (If only I had known!)

forms.en: He is only ten years old.

sentence.da: Jeg ville **blot** sige tak.
sentence.en: I just wanted to say thanks.

bly.explanation: "Et bly" means "lead", as in the metal. The ending "fri" means "free of", as in "blyfri" (lead-free) and "sukkerfri" (sugar-free).

sentence.da: Gamle rør kan være lavet af **bly**, som er giftigt.
sentence.en: Old pipes can be made of lead, which is poisonous.

blå.explanation: "Blå" means "blue". Put "lyse" (light) or "mørke" (dark) in front to make shades: "lyseblå" means "light blue" and "mørkeblå" means "dark blue".

sentence.da: Himlen er **blå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is blue today.

blæsende.explanation: "Blæsende" means "windy". It comes from "at blæse" (to blow). To say it is windy right now, say: "Det blæser" (It is windy).

sentence.da: Det var en **blæsende** dag ved havet.
sentence.en: It was a windy day by the sea.

blæst.explanation: "Blæst" means "a lot of wind". It comes from the verb "at blæse" (to blow).

sentence.da: Der er meget **blæst** på stranden i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of wind on the beach today.

blød.explanation: "Blød" means "soft". When you describe how a voice sounds, use it too: "en blød stemme" (a soft voice).

sentence.da: Jeg sover godt i en **blød** seng.
sentence.en: I sleep well in a soft bed.

blødende.explanation: "Blødende" means "bleeding". It comes from "at bløde" (to bleed).

sentence.da: Pres på det **blødende** sted, indtil blødningen stopper.
sentence.en: Press on the bleeding spot until the bleeding stops.

bogstavelig talt.explanation: "Bogstavelig talt" means "literally". It is built from "bogstavelig" (literal) and "talt" (spoken). To say something in a figure-of-speech way, use the opposite, "billedligt talt" (figuratively speaking): "Billedligt talt er han en løve" (Figuratively speaking, he is a lion).

sentence.da: Der var **bogstavelig talt** ingen mennesker på gaden, ikke en eneste.
sentence.en: There were literally no people in the street, not a single one.

bogstaveligt.explanation: "Bogstaveligt" means "literally". To say someone took your words exactly as said, use "at tage" (to take): "Hun tog min joke bogstaveligt" (She took my joke literally).

forms.da: Du skal ikke tage det bogstaveligt

sentence.da: Små børn forstår ofte ord **bogstaveligt**, så ironi er svær for dem.
sentence.en: Small children often understand words literally, so irony is hard for them.

boligmarkedet.explanation: "Boligmarkedet" means "the housing market". It is built from "en bolig" (a place to live) and "et marked" (a market). To say it is hard to start buying, say: "Det er svært at komme ind på boligmarkedet" (It is hard to get onto the housing market).

sentence.da: Priserne på **boligmarkedet** er steget meget i København.
sentence.en: Prices on the housing market have risen a lot in Copenhagen.

boligstøtte.explanation: "En boligstøtte" means "a housing benefit". It is built from "bolig" (home) and "støtte" (support). In Denmark there are two kinds: "boligsikring" (for most people) and "boligydelse" (for pensioners).

sentence.da: Staten giver **boligstøtte** til folk med lav indkomst og dyr husleje.
sentence.en: The state gives housing benefit to people with a low income and expensive rent.

boller i karry.explanation: "Boller i karry" means "meatballs in curry sauce". It is a classic Danish home-cooked dish. A single "bolle" means "a bun": "Jeg køber en bolle" (I buy a bun).

forms.en: meatballs in curry sauce with rice
a portion of meatballs in curry sauce

sentence.da: Jeg laver **boller i karry** af hakket svinekød og serverer dem med ris.
sentence.en: I make meatballs in curry sauce from minced pork and serve them with rice.

bomuld.explanation: "Bomuld" means "cotton". To ask in a shop what a shirt is made of: "Hvad er den lavet af?" "Den er lavet af bomuld." (What is it made of? It is made of cotton.)

sentence.da: Man dyrker **bomuld** i varme lande og laver tøj af det.
sentence.en: Cotton is grown in warm countries and clothes are made from it.

borgerservice.explanation: "Borgerservice" means "Citizen Services": the municipal office for practical matters like a health insurance card, a passport or registering your address. It is written with a capital B, like the name of an office.

forms.en: I have to go to Citizen Services.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have nyt pas på **Borgerservice**.
sentence.en: I need a new passport at Citizen Services.

bortset fra.explanation: "Bortset fra" means "apart from". To answer with an exception: "Er du klar?" "Ja, bortset fra skoene." (Are you ready? Yes, apart from my shoes.)

sentence.da: Alle kom **bortset fra** Lars.
sentence.en: Everyone came except Lars.

bravo.explanation: "Bravo" means "bravo". To cheer for good news: "Jeg har bestået eksamen!" "Bravo!" (I passed the exam! Bravo!)

sentence.da: **Bravo**, det var en flot koncert!
sentence.en: Bravo, that was a great concert!

bred.explanation: "Bred" means "wide". To say how wide something is, put the measure before it: "Vejen er ti meter bred" (The road is ten meters wide).

sentence.da: Vejen er **bred**, ikke smal.
sentence.en: The road is wide, not narrow.

briller.explanation: "Briller" means "glasses", as in the ones for your eyes. It always ends in "r", even for one pair: "Jeg har nye briller" (I have new glasses). To say you are wearing glasses, use "at have briller på" (to have glasses on): "Hun har briller på" (She has glasses on).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke læse uden mine **briller**.
sentence.en: I cannot read without my glasses.

brint.explanation: "Brint" means "hydrogen". To say a vehicle runs on it, use "på" (on): "Bussen kører på brint" (The bus runs on hydrogen).

sentence.da: Vand består af ilt og **brint**.
sentence.en: Water consists of oxygen and hydrogen.

britisk.explanation: "Britisk" means "British". Do not mix it up with "engelsk" (English), which is about England and the English language: "Jeg taler engelsk" (I speak English).

sentence.da: Han bor i London og er **britisk**.
sentence.en: He lives in London and is British.

broccoli.explanation: "En broccoli" means "a broccoli". To cook it in steam, use "at dampe" (to steam): "Jeg damper broccolien" (I steam the broccoli).

sentence.da: **Broccoli** er grøn og ligner et lille træ.
sentence.en: Broccoli is green and looks like a little tree.

brugbar.explanation: "Brugbar" means "usable". The ending "bar" means "able to be", as in "bærbar" (portable). Do not mix it up with "nyttig" (helpful), which describes something that helps you a lot: "en nyttig tip" (a helpful tip).

sentence.da: Cyklen er gammel, men den er stadig **brugbar**.
sentence.en: The bike is old, but it is still usable.

brugt.explanation: "Brugt" means "used". It comes from "at bruge" (to use). To say you bought something secondhand, put "brugt" after the thing: "Vi købte bilen brugt" (We bought the car used).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **brugt** cykel på nettet.
sentence.en: I bought a used bike online.

brun.explanation: "Brun" means "brown". It is also used for a suntan: "Du er blevet brun" (You have gotten a tan).

sentence.da: Chokolade er **brun**, ikke hvid.
sentence.en: Chocolate is brown, not white.

brunede kartofler.explanation: "Brunede kartofler" means "caramelized potatoes". In Denmark they are a traditional side dish for the Christmas roast. The name comes from the verb "at brune" (to brown).

sentence.da: Til julemaden laver vi **brunede kartofler** med sukker og smør.
sentence.en: For the Christmas meal we make caramelized potatoes with sugar and butter.

brutal.explanation: "Brutal" means "brutal". When you describe honesty that hurts, use it too: "brutal ærlighed" (brutal honesty).

sentence.da: Filmen var **brutal**, og mange vendte blikket væk.
sentence.en: The film was brutal, and many looked away.

brændende.explanation: "Brændende" means "burning". When you describe a strong wish, use it too: "et brændende ønske" (a burning wish).

sentence.da: De hentede børnene ud af det **brændende** hus og slukkede ilden.
sentence.en: They got the children out of the burning house and put out the fire.

brændstof.explanation: "Et brændstof" means "a fuel". It is built from "at brænde" (to burn) and "et stof" (a material). The ending "stof" is also in "et sprængstof" (an explosive).

sentence.da: Bilen bruger meget **brændstof** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car uses a lot of fuel on the highway.

brød.explanation: "Et brød" means "a loaf of bread". To say how many loaves, put the number before "brød" and leave the word unchanged: "to brød" (two loaves).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **brød** hos bageren.
sentence.en: I buy bread at the baker's.

buddhisme.explanation: "Buddhisme" means "Buddhism". Danish writes it with a lowercase "b", while English writes "Buddhism" with an uppercase "B".

sentence.da: I **buddhisme** er meditation en vigtig del af livet.
sentence.en: In Buddhism, meditation is an important part of life.

bukser.explanation: "Bukser" means "pants". To say how many pairs, use "par": "to par bukser" (two pairs of pants). The word always ends in "r", even for one pair: "Jeg har nye bukser" (I have new pants).

sentence.da: Jeg har **bukser** og sko på.
sentence.en: I am wearing pants and shoes.

bulgur.explanation: "Bulgur" means "bulgur". To answer what is for dinner: "Hvad skal vi have til aftensmad?" "Bulgur med grøntsager." (What are we having for dinner? Bulgur with vegetables.)

sentence.da: Jeg laver en salat af **bulgur**, tomat og persille.
sentence.en: I make a salad of bulgur, tomato and parsley.

buttet.explanation: "Buttet" means "chubby". Do not mix it up with "tyk" (thick or fat): "en tyk bog" (a thick book).

sentence.da: Den lille baby er **buttet**, og hans arme er bløde.
sentence.en: The little baby is chubby, and his arms are soft.

bydemåde.explanation: "En bydemåde" means "an imperative". It is built from "at byde" (to order) and "en måde" (a way), so it literally means "ordering way". Two examples of the imperative are "Kom her!" (Come here!) and "Hjælp mig!" (Help me!).

sentence.da: Sætningen Luk døren! står i **bydemåde**.
sentence.en: The sentence Close the door! is in the imperative.

byg.explanation: "Et byg" means "barley". The word is part of "byggryn" (pearl barley). The same spelling is also the order "Build!", from "at bygge" (to build): "Byg et hus!" (Build a house!).

sentence.da: Man bruger **byg** til at lave øl.
sentence.en: Barley is used to make beer.

byplanlægning.explanation: "Byplanlægning" means "urban planning". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "planlægning" (planning).

sentence.da: God **byplanlægning** gør det let at gå og cykle i byen.
sentence.en: Good urban planning makes it easy to walk and bike in the city.

byttepenge.explanation: "Byttepenge" means "change (money)". It comes from "at bytte" (to exchange) and "penge" (money). This word has no article, like "penge": "Jeg har ingen byttepenge" (I have no change).

sentence.da: Du får 20 kroner i **byttepenge**.
sentence.en: You get 20 kroner in change.

både…og.explanation: "Både … og" means "both … and". To say two things are true together, put "både" before the first and "og" before the second: "Det er både billigt og godt" (It is both cheap and good).

forms.da: både i dag og i morgen

sentence.da: Hun taler **både** dansk **og** engelsk.
sentence.en: She speaks both Danish and English.

bærbar.explanation: "Bærbar" means "portable". When you talk about a laptop, you can leave out "computer" and say just "en bærbar": "Jeg har købt en ny bærbar" (I bought a new laptop).

sentence.da: Min computer er **bærbar** og let at tage med.
sentence.en: My computer is portable and easy to take along.

bæredygtig.explanation: "Bæredygtig" means "sustainable". It is built from "at bære" (to carry) and "dygtig" (able), so it literally means "able to carry".

sentence.da: En **bæredygtig** løsning kan holde i mange år uden at ødelægge naturen.
sentence.en: A sustainable solution can last for many years without destroying nature.

bæredygtighed.explanation: "Bæredygtighed" means "sustainability". Do not mix it up with "bæredygtig" (sustainable), which describes a choice or a product: "en bæredygtig løsning" (a sustainable solution).

sentence.da: Eleverne lærer om **bæredygtighed** og om at passe på naturen.
sentence.en: The students learn about sustainability and about taking care of nature.

bønner.explanation: "En bønne" means "a bean". The plural "bønner" also means "prayers", from "en bøn" (a prayer): "Mine bønner blev hørt" (My prayers were heard).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **bønner** og majs til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I eat beans and corn for dinner.

børnepasning.explanation: "Børnepasning" means "childcare". It is built from "børn" (children) and "pasning" (care). In Denmark the municipality arranges it and parents pay part of the cost.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for **børnepasning**, fordi begge forældre arbejder.
sentence.en: We need childcare because both parents work.

en baby.explanation: "En baby" means "a baby". To say a couple is going to have one, use "at vente" (to wait): "Vi venter en baby" (We are expecting a baby).

sentence.da: Vores **baby** er to måneder gammel.
sentence.en: Our baby is two months old.

en babyalarm.explanation: "En babyalarm" means "a baby monitor". It is built from "en baby" (a baby) and "en alarm" (an alarm). To say you switch it on, use "at tænde" (to turn on): "Jeg tænder babyalarmen" (I turn on the baby monitor).

sentence.da: Med en **babyalarm** kan vi høre barnet, når vi er i stuen.
sentence.en: With a baby monitor we can hear the child when we are in the living room.

en babysitter.explanation: "En babysitter" means "a babysitter". To say you have arranged one, use "at få" (to get): "Vi har fået en babysitter i aften" (We have a babysitter tonight).

sentence.da: En **babysitter** passer børnene, når vi er ude.
sentence.en: A babysitter looks after the children when we are out.

en bachelor.explanation: "En bachelor" means "a bachelor's degree". To say you are studying for one, use "at læse" (to study): "Hun læser en bachelor i historie" (She is studying for a bachelor's degree in history). To say an unmarried man, use "en ungkarl" (an unmarried man): "Min onkel er ungkarl" (My uncle is an unmarried man).

sentence.da: Efter min **bachelor** læser jeg videre til en kandidat.
sentence.en: After my bachelor's I keep studying toward a master's.

en backup.explanation: "En backup" means "a backup". To say you get your files back, use "at gendanne" (to restore) with "fra" (from): "Jeg gendanner mine filer fra en backup" (I restore my files from a backup).

sentence.da: Jeg har lavet en **backup** af alle mine billeder.
sentence.en: I made a backup of all my pictures.

en badedragt.explanation: "En badedragt" means "a swimsuit". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en dragt" (a suit). To say you put it on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager badedragten på" (I put on my swimsuit).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have min **badedragt** med til poolen.
sentence.en: I need to bring my swimsuit to the pool.

en bademåtte.explanation: "En bademåtte" means "a bath mat". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en måtte" (a mat). The part "måtte" (mat) is also in "en gulvmåtte" (a floor mat).

sentence.da: Husk at lægge en **bademåtte** foran badekarret.
sentence.en: Remember to put a bath mat in front of the bathtub.

en badestrand.explanation: "En badestrand" means "a bathing beach". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en strand" (a beach). To say you swim in the sea, use "at bade" (to swim): "Vi bader i havet hele sommeren" (We swim in the sea all summer).

sentence.da: Vi svømmer hver dag ved en lille **badestrand**.
sentence.en: We swim every day at a small bathing beach.

en badevægt.explanation: "En badevægt" means "a bathroom scale". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en vægt" (a weight). To say you step on it, use "at stå på" (to stand on): "Jeg står på badevægten hver morgen" (I step on the bathroom scale every morning).

sentence.da: Min **badevægt** viser, at jeg har tabt mig to kilo.
sentence.en: My bathroom scale shows that I have lost two kilos.

en bagagebærer.explanation: "En bagagebærer" means "a luggage rack or bike rack". It is built from "en bagage" (luggage) and "at bære" (to carry). To say you fasten a bag to the back of a bike, use "at spænde fast" (to strap on): "Jeg spænder tasken fast på bagagebæreren" (I strap the bag onto the rack).

sentence.da: Min cykel har en **bagagebærer** til tasken.
sentence.en: My bike has a rack for the bag.

en bageplade.explanation: "En bageplade" means "a baking tray". It is built from "at bage" (to bake) and "en plade" (a sheet). To say you cover it so nothing sticks, use "bagepapir" (baking paper): "Læg bagepapir på bagepladen" (Put baking paper on the baking tray).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger kagerne på en **bageplade** og sætter den i ovnen.
sentence.en: I put the cakes on a baking tray and put it in the oven.

en bager.explanation: "En bager" means "a baker". It comes from "at bage" (to bake). To say you go to the bakery, Danish names the person instead of the shop: "Jeg går til bageren" (I am going to the bakery), literally "I am going to the baker".

sentence.da: En **bager** laver brød hver morgen.
sentence.en: A baker makes bread every morning.

en baggrund.explanation: "En baggrund" means "a background". To say what is behind the main part of a picture or a scene, use "i baggrunden" (in the background): "Man kan se bjerge i baggrunden" (You can see mountains in the background). To talk about a person's past, such as their education and life so far, it also means "background": "Hun har en anden baggrund" (She has a different background).

sentence.da: Billedet har en blå **baggrund**.
sentence.en: The picture has a blue background.

en baggård.explanation: "En baggård" means "a backyard". It is built from "bag" (behind) and "en gård" (a yard). To talk about a farm, the same word "gård" is used: "Han bor på en gård" (He lives on a farm).

sentence.da: Børnene leger i en **baggård** mellem husene.
sentence.en: The children play in a backyard between the houses.

en baglygte.explanation: "En baglygte" means "a taillight". It is built from "bag" (back) and "en lygte" (a light). To tell someone to switch it on, use "at tænde" (to switch on): "Husk at tænde baglygten på cyklen" (Remember to switch on the taillight on the bike).

sentence.da: Din **baglygte** er rød, men forlygten er hvid.
sentence.en: Your taillight is red, but the headlight is white.

en bagning.explanation: "En bagning" means "a baking". It comes from "at bage" (to bake). The ending "-ning" turns a verb into a noun in many words, such as "en tegning" (a drawing) from "at tegne" (to draw).

sentence.da: Efter **bagning** dufter hele huset af friske boller.
sentence.en: After baking, the whole house smells of fresh rolls.

en bagside.explanation: "En bagside" means "a back or downside". When you point to the rear of a page, a card or an envelope, it means "back": "Bagsiden af kuverten er tom" (The back of the envelope is empty). When you talk about the unwelcome part of something good, it means "downside": "Det er medaljens bagside" (That is the flip side of the medal).

sentence.da: Skriv navnet på kortets **bagside**.
sentence.en: Write the name on the back of the card.

en baguette.explanation: "En baguette" means "a baguette". To say what is in it, use "med" (with): "en baguette med ost" (a baguette with cheese).

sentence.da: En **baguette** er et langt, tyndt brød fra Frankrig.
sentence.en: A baguette is a long, thin bread from France.

en bakke.explanation: "En bakke" means "a hill". When you carry cups or plates on a flat board with a rim, it also means "a tray": "Jeg bærer en bakke med kaffe" (I carry a tray with coffee).

sentence.da: Det er hårdt at cykle op ad en **bakke**.
sentence.en: It is hard to bike up a hill.

en bakterie.explanation: "En bakterie" means "a bacterium". Spell it with a "k", not a "c" as in English. To say soap kills germs, use "at dræbe" (to kill): "Sæbe dræber bakterier" (Soap kills bacteria).

sentence.da: En **bakterie** er for lille til at se uden mikroskop.
sentence.en: A bacterium is too small to see without a microscope.

en balance.explanation: "En balance" means "a balance", being steady or even. For the money in a bank account, use "en saldo" (a balance): "Min saldo er 500 kroner" (My balance is 500 kroner).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at finde en **balance** mellem arbejde og fritid.
sentence.en: It is important to find a balance between work and free time.

en balje.explanation: "En balje" means "a tub". To talk about the tub you wash dishes in, add "opvaske" (washing-up): "Jeg skyller glassene i opvaskebaljen" (I rinse the glasses in the washing-up bowl).

sentence.da: Hun vasker tøjet i en **balje** med varmt vand.
sentence.en: She washes the clothes in a tub with warm water.

en balkon.explanation: "En balkon" means "a balcony". To say where you are sitting, use "på" (on): "Jeg sidder på balkonen" (I am sitting on the balcony).

sentence.da: Vores lejlighed har en lille **balkon** mod gaden.
sentence.en: Our apartment has a small balcony facing the street.

en ballet.explanation: "En ballet" means "a ballet". To say someone does ballet as a dancer, use "at danse ballet" (to dance ballet) without "en": "Hun danser ballet" (She dances ballet).

sentence.da: I en **ballet** fortæller danserne en historie uden ord.
sentence.en: In a ballet the dancers tell a story without words.

en ballon.explanation: "En ballon" means "a balloon". To say you fill a balloon with air, use "at puste op" (to blow up): "Jeg puster ballonen op" (I blow up the balloon).

sentence.da: En **ballon** er fuld af luft.
sentence.en: A balloon is full of air.

en bamse.explanation: "En bamse" means "a teddy bear". When you describe a big, gentle, cuddly person, it also means "a teddy bear": "Han er en rigtig bamse" (He is a real teddy bear).

sentence.da: Min datter sover med sin **bamse**.
sentence.en: My daughter sleeps with her teddy bear.

en banan.explanation: "En banan" means "a banana". To say you take the skin off, use "at skrælle" (to peel): "Jeg skræller en banan" (I peel a banana).

sentence.da: Aben spiser en gul **banan**.
sentence.en: The monkey eats a yellow banana.

en bandage.explanation: "En bandage" means "a bandage". For a small sticky one on a cut, use "et plaster" (an adhesive bandage): "Jeg sætter et plaster på fingeren" (I put an adhesive bandage on my finger).

sentence.da: En **bandage** beskytter såret og holder det rent.
sentence.en: A bandage protects the wound and keeps it clean.

en bande.explanation: "En bande" means "a gang". When you talk about a group of friends, it also means "gang": "Hele banden kommer" (The whole gang is coming).

sentence.da: Politiet har anholdt en **bande**, som stjal biler.
sentence.en: The police have arrested a gang that stole cars.

en bane.explanation: "En bane" means "a court", as in a sports court. When you talk about the path that runners run along or trains travel on, it also means "a track": "Løberne står klar på banen" (The runners are ready on the track).

sentence.da: Vi spiller fodbold på en ny **bane** ved skolen.
sentence.en: We play soccer on a new field by the school.

en banegård.explanation: "En banegård" means "a railway station". It is built from "en bane" (a railway line) and "en gård" (a yard). To name the main station of a Danish city, "hoved" (main) goes in front: "Københavns Hovedbanegård" (Copenhagen Central Station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en stor **banegård**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a big railway station.

en bank.explanation: "En bank" means "a bank", as in the place for money. To say you are going to the bank, use "i" (in): "Jeg går i banken i dag" (I am going to the bank today).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter mine penge ind i en **bank**.
sentence.en: I put my money into a bank.

en bankkonto.explanation: "En bankkonto" means "a bank account". It is built from "en bank" (a bank) and "en konto" (an account). To say you open one, use "at oprette" (to set up): "Jeg vil gerne oprette en bankkonto" (I would like to open a bank account).

sentence.da: Jeg har penge på min **bankkonto**.
sentence.en: I have money in my bank account.

en bankrådgiver.explanation: "En bankrådgiver" means "a bank adviser". It is built from "en bank" (a bank) and "en rådgiver" (an adviser). To say you are meeting one, use "et møde med" (a meeting with): "Jeg har et møde med min bankrådgiver" (I have a meeting with my bank adviser).

sentence.da: Min **bankrådgiver** hjælper mig, når jeg skal låne penge.
sentence.en: My bank adviser helps me when I need to borrow money.

en barbermaskine.explanation: "En barbermaskine" means "an electric shaver". It is built from "at barbere" (to shave) and "en maskine" (a machine). For a razor you use by hand, say "en barberhøvl" (a razor): "Jeg køber en ny barberhøvl" (I am buying a new razor).

sentence.da: Han barberer sig hver morgen med en **barbermaskine**.
sentence.en: He shaves every morning with an electric shaver.

en barista.explanation: "En barista" means "a barista". Do not mix it up with "en bartender" (a bartender). To talk about the person who makes coffee, say: "Baristaen laver en cappuccino" (The barista makes a cappuccino). To talk about the person who makes mixed drinks, say: "Bartenderen laver en cocktail" (The bartender makes a cocktail).

sentence.da: En **barista** er uddannet til at lave god kaffe.
sentence.en: A barista is trained to make good coffee.

en barndom.explanation: "En barndom" means "a childhood". To say something happened when you were young, use "i" (in) before "min barndom" (my childhood): "I min barndom boede vi på landet" (In my childhood we lived in the country).

sentence.da: Jeg tænker ofte på min **barndom** hos mormor.
sentence.en: I often think of my childhood at Grandma's house.

en barndomsven.explanation: "En barndomsven" means "a childhood friend". It is built from "en barndom" (a childhood) and "en ven" (a friend). To talk about a woman or girl, use "en barndomsveninde" (a female childhood friend): "Hun er min barndomsveninde" (She is my childhood friend).

sentence.da: Han er min **barndomsven** fra børnehaven.
sentence.en: He is my childhood friend from kindergarten.

en barnedåb.explanation: "En barnedåb" means "a christening". It is built from "et barn" (a child) and "en dåb" (a baptism). To say a baby is christened, use "at døbe" (to baptize): "Vi skal døbe babyen i kirken i morgen" (We are going to christen the baby in the church tomorrow).

sentence.da: Ved en **barnedåb** får barnet sit navn i kirken.
sentence.en: At a christening, the child gets its name in the church.

en barnepige.explanation: "En barnepige" means "a nanny or babysitter". It is built from "et barn" (a child) and "en pige" (a girl). To say you are the babysitter for someone, use "at være barnepige for" (to be a babysitter for): "Jeg er barnepige for min niece" (I am the babysitter for my niece).

sentence.da: Vores **barnepige** passer børnene i aften.
sentence.en: Our nanny is looking after the children tonight.

en barnevogn.explanation: "En barnevogn" means "a baby carriage". To say you take the baby for a walk, use "at gå en tur med" (to go for a walk with): "Jeg går en tur med barnevognen" (I am going for a walk with the baby carriage).

sentence.da: Hun skubber en **barnevogn** ned ad gaden.
sentence.en: She pushes a baby carriage down the street.

en bartender.explanation: "En bartender" means "a bartender". Another word for the same job is "en barmand" (a barman): "Barmanden smiler til gæsterne" (The barman smiles at the guests).

sentence.da: En **bartender** blander drinks og skænker øl i baren.
sentence.en: A bartender mixes drinks and pours beer at the bar.

en base.explanation: "En base" means "a base", as in a military base. In chemistry, it means a substance that reacts with an acid: "En base kan neutralisere en syre" (A base can neutralize an acid). For the bottom of an object, use "en bund" (a bottom): "Der er vand i bunden af flasken" (There is water in the bottom of the bottle).

sentence.da: Soldaterne bor på en **base** tæt på grænsen.
sentence.en: The soldiers live on a base close to the border.

en bedrager.explanation: "En bedrager" means "a con artist". It comes from "at bedrage" (to deceive). To talk about the crime, use "bedrageri" (fraud): "Han blev dømt for bedrageri" (He was convicted of fraud).

sentence.da: En **bedrager** lyver for at få andres penge.
sentence.en: A con artist lies to get other people's money.

en bedrift.explanation: "En bedrift" means "an achievement or feat". To say someone did something impressive, say: "Hans bedrift blev fejret af hele landet" (His achievement was celebrated by the whole country). When you talk about a business, it also means "business", as in "en landbrugsbedrift" (a farm business).

sentence.da: At bestige Mount Everest uden ilt er en stor **bedrift**.
sentence.en: Climbing Mount Everest without oxygen is a great feat.

en bedstefar.explanation: "En bedstefar" means "a grandfather". To say he is your mother's father, use "morfar": "Min morfar er pensionist" (My mother's father is retired). To say he is your father's father, use "farfar": "Min farfar bor i Odense" (My father's father lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **bedstefar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en bedstemor.explanation: "En bedstemor" means "a grandmother". To say she is your mother's mother, use "mormor": "Min mormor bager boller" (My mother's mother bakes buns). To say she is your father's mother, use "farmor": "Min farmor bor i Odense" (My father's mother lives in Odense).

sentence.da: Min **bedstemor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en bedømmelse.explanation: "En bedømmelse" means "an assessment". It comes from "at bedømme" (to judge). To say you receive one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en god bedømmelse" (I got a good assessment).

sentence.da: Læreren giver en **bedømmelse** af, hvor god opgaven er.
sentence.en: The teacher gives an assessment of how good the assignment is.

en bedøvelse.explanation: "En bedøvelse" means "an anesthetic". To say someone is under general anesthesia for surgery, use "narkose" (general anesthesia) with "i" (in): "Hun er i narkose" (She is under general anesthesia).

sentence.da: Tandlægen gav mig en **bedøvelse**, så det ikke gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: The dentist gave me an anesthetic so that it did not hurt.

en befolkning.explanation: "En befolkning" means "a population". To say the number of people is rising, use "at vokse" (to grow): "Befolkningen vokser hvert år" (The population grows every year). To talk about one person living in a town, use "en indbygger" (an inhabitant): "Byen har 50.000 indbyggere" (The town has 50,000 inhabitants).

sentence.da: Danmarks **befolkning** er næsten seks millioner mennesker.
sentence.en: Denmark's population is almost six million people.

en befrielse.explanation: "En befrielse" means "a liberation". In Denmark, "Befrielsen" (the Liberation) is the name for the end of the German occupation in May 1945. When you feel a burden is gone, it also means "relief": "Det var en befrielse at aflevere opgaven" (It was a relief to hand in the assignment).

sentence.da: Efter krigen fik landet sin **befrielse**, og folk dansede på gaden.
sentence.en: After the war the country got its liberation, and people danced in the street.

en begavelse.explanation: "En begavelse" means "a talent". It comes from "begavet" (gifted). To say someone has great talent, use "stor" (great): "Hun har en stor begavelse" (She has a great talent).

sentence.da: Hendes **begavelse** viste sig tidligt, fordi hun kunne læse som treårig.
sentence.en: Her talent showed early, because she could read at age three.

en begivenhed.explanation: "En begivenhed" means "an event". To say an event takes place, use "at finde sted" (to take place): "Begivenheden finder sted i morgen" (The event takes place tomorrow).

sentence.da: Festivalen er en stor **begivenhed** i byen.
sentence.en: The festival is a big event in the town.

en begravelse.explanation: "En begravelse" means "a funeral". To say you attend one, use "at deltage i" (to take part in): "Vi deltager i begravelsen" (We are attending the funeral).

sentence.da: Der er en **begravelse** i kirken på lørdag.
sentence.en: There is a funeral in the church on Saturday.

en begrundelse.explanation: "En begrundelse" means "a justification". It is built on "en grund" (a reason). To ask for the reason behind something, say: "Hvad er begrundelsen?" (What is the reason?)

sentence.da: Hvis du siger nej, skal du give en **begrundelse**.
sentence.en: If you say no, you must give a justification.

en begrænsning.explanation: "En begrænsning" means "a limitation". It is built on "en grænse" (a border or limit). To say there are no limits, use "ingen" (no): "Der er ingen begrænsninger" (There are no limitations).

sentence.da: Manglende plads er en stor **begrænsning** i en lille lejlighed.
sentence.en: A lack of space is a big limitation in a small apartment.

en begyndelse.explanation: "En begyndelse" means "a beginning". It is built from "at begynde" (to begin). To say it happens in the first part of something, use "i begyndelsen af" (at the beginning of): "I begyndelsen af filmen er der en storm" (At the beginning of the film there is a storm).

sentence.da: Et eventyr har en **begyndelse** og en slutning.
sentence.en: A fairy tale has a beginning and an ending.

en begynder.explanation: "En begynder" means "a beginner". It comes from "at begynde" (to begin). To talk about a class for beginners, use "et begynderhold" (a beginners' class): "Jeg går på et begynderhold" (I am in a beginners' class).

sentence.da: Jeg er kun **begynder**, men jeg lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: I am only a beginner, but I learn fast.

en behandling.explanation: "En behandling" means "a treatment". It comes from "at behandle" (to treat). When you talk about how someone is treated, it also means "treatment": "Han fik dårlig behandling" (He got bad treatment).

sentence.da: Hun er syg og får **behandling** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: She is sick and is getting treatment at the hospital.

en bekendt.explanation: "En bekendt" means "an acquaintance". To say someone is not a close friend, say: "Han er en bekendt, ikke en nær ven" (He is an acquaintance, not a close friend). When a song or a face seems known to you, the adjective "bekendt" means "familiar": "Sangen lyder bekendt" (The song sounds familiar).

sentence.da: Jeg mødte en **bekendt** i byen.
sentence.en: I met an acquaintance in town.

en bekendtgørelse.explanation: "En bekendtgørelse" means "an announcement or regulation". It is built from "bekendt" (known) and "at gøre" (to make): it makes something known. In Denmark, a minister issues a "bekendtgørelse" to set out the details of how a law works.

sentence.da: Ministeriet har udsendt en **bekendtgørelse** om nye regler for taxaer.
sentence.en: The ministry has issued a regulation about new rules for taxis.

en bekymring.explanation: "En bekymring" means "a worry". To say you worry, use "at bekymre sig" (literally, to worry yourself): "Jeg bekymrer mig" (I worry). To say you are worried about someone, use the adjective "bekymret" (worried): "Hun er bekymret for sin søn" (She is worried about her son).

sentence.da: Min største **bekymring** er pengene.
sentence.en: My biggest worry is the money.

en belastning.explanation: "En belastning" means "a strain". It comes from "at belaste" (to put a load on). To take the strain off someone, use "at aflaste" (to relieve): "Jeg aflaster dig i dag" (I am relieving you today).

sentence.da: Lange arbejdsdage er en stor **belastning** for kroppen.
sentence.en: Long workdays are a big strain on the body.

en belønning.explanation: "En belønning" means "a reward". To say what you get as a reward, use "som" (as): "Du får en is som belønning" (You get an ice cream as a reward).

sentence.da: Du får en **belønning**, når du er færdig.
sentence.en: You get a reward when you are done.

en benzinstation.explanation: "En benzinstation" means "a gas station". It is built from "benzin" (gasoline) and "en station" (a station). To say you fill the car with fuel, use "at tanke" (to fill up): "Jeg skal tanke på benzinstationen" (I need to fill up at the gas station).

sentence.da: Tanken er næsten tom, og vi skal til en **benzinstation**.
sentence.en: The tank is almost empty, and we have to go to a gas station.

en beregning.explanation: "En beregning" means "a calculation". To say you work something out, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en beregning af prisen" (I am making a calculation of the price). Do not mix it up with "en regning" (a bill): "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill).

sentence.da: Min **beregning** viser, at turen koster otte hundrede kroner.
sentence.en: My calculation shows that the trip costs eight hundred kroner.

en bersærk.explanation: "En bersærk" means "a berserker". Danish spells it with "æ", where English has "berserk". To say someone loses control in anger, use "at gå bersærk" (to go berserk): "Han gik bersærk i butikken" (He went berserk in the shop).

sentence.da: I de gamle sagaer kæmper en **bersærk** vildt og føler ingen smerte.
sentence.en: In the old sagas, a berserker fights wildly and feels no pain.

en berøring.explanation: "En berøring" means "a touch". It comes from "at berøre" (to touch): "Han berørte min arm" (He touched my arm). To describe a gentle one, add "blid" (gentle): "en blid berøring" (a gentle touch).

sentence.da: Mimosaen lukker sine blade ved den mindste **berøring**.
sentence.en: The mimosa closes its leaves at the slightest touch.

en besiddelse.explanation: "En besiddelse" means "a possession". To talk about a person's belongings, use the plural: "personlige besiddelser" (personal belongings). When you talk about having something illegal on you, it also means "possession": "besiddelse af stoffer" (possession of drugs).

sentence.da: Hans eneste **besiddelse** var en gammel cykel.
sentence.en: His only possession was an old bike.

en besked.explanation: "En besked" means "a message". To ask someone to let you know, use "at give besked" (to let someone know): "Giv mig besked i morgen" (Let me know tomorrow). To say you were told something, use "at få besked" (to get word): "Jeg fik besked om mødet" (I was told about the meeting).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **besked** til dig fra Anna.
sentence.en: I have a message for you from Anna.

en beskrivelse.explanation: "En beskrivelse" means "a description". It comes from "at beskrive" (to describe). To tell someone to write a short one, use "kort" (short): "Skriv en kort beskrivelse" (Write a short description).

sentence.da: Politiet bad om en **beskrivelse** af manden, der løb væk.
sentence.en: The police asked for a description of the man who ran away.

en beskyldning.explanation: "En beskyldning" means "an accusation". It comes from "at beskylde" (to accuse). To say someone makes one, use "at komme med" (to come out with): "Han kom med en beskyldning mod mig" (He made an accusation against me).

sentence.da: En **beskyldning** uden beviser kan skade en uskyldig.
sentence.en: An accusation without proof can harm an innocent person.

en beskæresaks.explanation: "En beskæresaks" means "a pair of pruning shears". It is built from "at beskære" (to prune) and "en saks" (scissors). To say you cut a hedge back, use "at beskære": "Jeg beskærer hækken i april" (I prune the hedge in April).

sentence.da: Med en **beskæresaks** kan man klippe tykke grene af.
sentence.en: With pruning shears you can cut off thick branches.

en beslutning.explanation: "En beslutning" means "a decision". To say you make one, use "at træffe" (to make): "Vi træffer en beslutning" (We make a decision).

sentence.da: Det var en svær **beslutning** at flytte til udlandet.
sentence.en: It was a hard decision to move abroad.

en beslutningsproces.explanation: "En beslutningsproces" means "a decision-making process". It is built from "en beslutning" (a decision) and "en proces" (a process). To say people take part, use "med i" (in on): "Medarbejderne er med i beslutningsprocessen" (The employees take part in the decision-making process).

sentence.da: En **beslutningsproces** tager tid, fordi mange skal høres.
sentence.en: A decision-making process takes time because many people must be heard.

en beslutningstager.explanation: "En beslutningstager" means "a decision-maker". It is built from "en beslutning" (a decision) and "at tage" (to take). To say who has the last word, add "endelig" (final): "Direktøren er den endelige beslutningstager" (The director is the final decision-maker).

sentence.da: En **beslutningstager** har det sidste ord i sagen.
sentence.en: A decision-maker has the last word in the matter.

en bestemmelse.explanation: "En bestemmelse" means "a provision". It comes from "at bestemme" (to decide). To say what a provision requires, use "ifølge" (according to): "Ifølge bestemmelsen skal du betale i dag" (According to the provision, you must pay today).

sentence.da: I kontrakten står der en **bestemmelse** om, hvem der betaler.
sentence.en: The contract has a provision about who pays.

en bestilling.explanation: "En bestilling" means "an order", as in an order placed in a shop. It comes from "at bestille" (to order). To ask whether an order has arrived, say: "Har du modtaget min bestilling?" (Have you received my order?)

sentence.da: Din **bestilling** er sendt, og den kommer i morgen.
sentence.en: Your order has been sent, and it is coming tomorrow.

en bestseller.explanation: "En bestseller" means "a bestseller". To say a book is among the best-selling ones, use "en bestsellerliste" (a bestseller list): "Bogen ligger på bestsellerlisten" (The book is on the bestseller list).

sentence.da: Hendes bog blev en **bestseller** og solgte over en million eksemplarer.
sentence.en: Her book became a bestseller and sold over a million copies.

en bestyrelse.explanation: "En bestyrelse" means "a board", as in the group that leads a company or an association. To say you are a member, use "at sidde i" (to sit in): "Hun sidder i bestyrelsen" (She is on the board).

sentence.da: Foreningen har en **bestyrelse**, som vælges hvert år.
sentence.en: The association has a board that is elected every year.

en besætning.explanation: "En besætning" means "a crew", as in the people working on a ship or a plane. On a farm, it also means all the animals kept there: "en kvægbesætning" (a herd of cattle).

sentence.da: En **besætning** arbejder på skibet, mens passagererne rejser.
sentence.en: A crew works on the ship while the passengers travel.

en besættelse.explanation: "En besættelse" means "an occupation", as in an army taking over a country (never a job). In Denmark, "besættelsen" (the occupation) is the name for the German occupation from 1940 to 1945. When you cannot stop thinking about something, it also means "obsession": "Det er blevet en besættelse for ham" (It has become an obsession for him).

sentence.da: Hans **besættelse** af tal tager al hans tid.
sentence.en: His obsession with numbers takes all his time.

en besøgende.explanation: "En besøgende" means "a visitor". It comes from "at besøge" (to visit). To say something is for the visitors, use "til" (for): "Der er gratis kaffe til de besøgende" (There is free coffee for the visitors).

sentence.da: Der er mange **besøgende** på museet i dag.
sentence.en: There are many visitors at the museum today.

en betaling.explanation: "En betaling" means "a payment". To say how you pay, use "med" (by): "betaling med kort" (payment by card).

sentence.da: Vi har modtaget din **betaling**, tak.
sentence.en: We have received your payment, thanks.

en betalingsmetode.explanation: "En betalingsmetode" means "a payment method". It is built from "en betaling" (a payment) and "en metode" (a method). In Denmark, "MobilePay" (a Danish phone payment app) is one payment method.

sentence.da: Du skal vælge en **betalingsmetode**, før du kan købe varen.
sentence.en: You must choose a payment method before you can buy the item.

en betingelse.explanation: "En betingelse" means "a condition", as in something that must be true first. For how a person or thing is doing, such as health, use "en tilstand" (a state): "Patientens tilstand er god" (The patient's condition is good).

sentence.da: Du får lånet på én **betingelse**: du skal betale til tiden.
sentence.en: You get the loan on one condition: you must pay on time.

en betjent.explanation: "En betjent" means "a police officer". A longer word for the same job is "en politibetjent" (a police officer). To say what an officer does on the road, say: "Betjenten standser bilen" (The officer stops the car).

sentence.da: En **betjent** arbejder for politiet og holder styr på trafikken.
sentence.en: A police officer works for the police and controls traffic.

en betragtning.explanation: "En betragtning" means "a consideration". To share your thoughts on a matter, use the plural: "Jeg har nogle betragtninger om sagen" (I have some thoughts on the matter).

sentence.da: Prisen er en vigtig **betragtning**, når vi vælger et sted at bo.
sentence.en: The price is an important consideration when we choose a place to live.

en betydning.explanation: "En betydning" means "a meaning". When something matters, it also means "importance": "Det har stor betydning" (It matters a lot).

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **betydning**.
sentence.en: I don't know the meaning of the word.

en betændelse.explanation: "En betændelse" means "an inflammation". When you talk about an infection, it also means "infection": "en betændelse i øret" (an ear infection).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **betændelse** i halsen, så det gør ondt at synke.
sentence.en: I have an inflammation in my throat, so it hurts to swallow.

en beundrer.explanation: "En beundrer" means "an admirer". It comes from "at beundre" (to admire). To talk about someone who is secretly in love with you, add "hemmelig" (secret): "en hemmelig beundrer" (a secret admirer).

sentence.da: Hun er en stor **beundrer** af Karen Blixens bøger.
sentence.en: She is a great admirer of Karen Blixen's books.

en bevilling.explanation: "En bevilling" means "a grant", as in money from an authority or a fund. When you talk about an official permit, it also means "permit": "en bevilling til at sælge alkohol" (a permit to sell alcohol).

sentence.da: Forskerne fik en **bevilling** på en million kroner til projektet.
sentence.en: The researchers got a grant of a million kroner for the project.

en bevægelse.explanation: "En bevægelse" means "a movement". To say something is in motion, use "i" (in): "Toget er i bevægelse" (The train is in motion). When you talk about a group working for a cause, it also means "movement": "arbejderbevægelsen" (the labor movement).

sentence.da: Hun lavede en hurtig **bevægelse** med hånden.
sentence.en: She made a quick movement with her hand.

en bh.explanation: "En bh" means "a bra". To say you put one on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Hun tager sin bh på" (She puts on her bra).

sentence.da: En **bh** er en slags undertøj til kvinder.
sentence.en: A bra is a kind of underwear for women.

en bi.explanation: "En bi" means "a bee". To say a bee stung you, use "at stikke" (to sting): "Jeg blev stukket af en bi" (I was stung by a bee).

sentence.da: En **bi** summer rundt om blomsten.
sentence.en: A bee buzzes around the flower.

en biavler.explanation: "En biavler" means "a beekeeper". It is built from "en bi" (a bee) and "at avle" (to breed). To say someone keeps bees, use "at holde bier" (to keep bees): "Min nabo holder bier" (My neighbor keeps bees).

sentence.da: En **biavler** passer bikuber og sælger honning på markedet.
sentence.en: A beekeeper looks after beehives and sells honey at the market.

en bibel.explanation: "En bibel" means "a bible". When you call a book the main guide in a field, it also means "bible": "Bogen er kokkenes bibel" (The book is the chefs' bible).

sentence.da: En **bibel** består af Det Gamle og Det Nye Testamente.
sentence.en: A bible consists of the Old and the New Testament.

en bibliotekar.explanation: "En bibliotekar" means "a librarian". The ending "-ar" also makes a word for a person in "en arkivar" (an archivist): "Arkivaren finder gamle papirer" (The archivist finds old papers).

sentence.da: Spørg en **bibliotekar**, hvis du ikke kan finde bogen.
sentence.en: Ask a librarian if you cannot find the book.

en bid.explanation: "En bid" means "a bite" of food. To name the food, put its name after "bid": "en bid brød" (a bite of bread).

sentence.da: Vil du have en **bid** af min kage?
sentence.en: Do you want a bite of my cake?

en bidragyder.explanation: "En bidragyder" means "a contributor". It is built from "et bidrag" (a contribution) and "at yde" (to provide). To say someone gives a lot, add "stor" (big): "Firmaet er en stor bidragyder" (The company is a major contributor).

sentence.da: Museet takker hver **bidragyder** til den nye udstilling.
sentence.en: The museum thanks every contributor to the new exhibition.

en bikini.explanation: "En bikini" means "a bikini". For a one-piece swimsuit, use "en badedragt" (a swimsuit): "Hun har en badedragt på" (She is wearing a swimsuit).

sentence.da: På stranden har hun en rød **bikini** på.
sentence.en: On the beach she is wearing a red bikini.

en bil.explanation: "En bil" means "a car". To say you go by car, use "i bil" (by car), without "en": "Vi kører i bil til Aarhus" (We are going to Aarhus by car).

sentence.da: En **bil** har fire hjul og en motor.
sentence.en: A car has four wheels and an engine.

en bilist.explanation: "En bilist" means "a motorist". It is built from "en bil" (a car) and "-ist". The ending "-ist" makes a word for a person in "en pianist" (a pianist) and "en turist" (a tourist).

sentence.da: En **bilist** skal altid holde tilbage for fodgængere.
sentence.en: A motorist must always yield to pedestrians.

en bille.explanation: "En bille" means "a beetle". The ending "bille" is also in names of kinds of beetle, as in "en løbebille" (a ground beetle).

sentence.da: En **bille** har et hårdt skjold på ryggen.
sentence.en: A beetle has a hard shield on its back.

en billedhugger.explanation: "En billedhugger" means "a sculptor". It is built from "et billede" (a picture) and "at hugge" (to chop), so literally it is a picture chopper.

sentence.da: En **billedhugger** laver figurer af sten og ler.
sentence.en: A sculptor makes figures out of stone and clay.

en billet.explanation: "En billet" means "a ticket". A very common phrase is "at bestille en billet" (to book a ticket): "Vi har bestilt billetter til koncerten" (We have booked tickets for the concert).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **billet** til toget.
sentence.en: I have bought a ticket for the train.

en billetautomat.explanation: "En billetautomat" means "a ticket machine". It is built from "billet" (ticket) and "automat" (machine).

sentence.da: Du kan købe en billet ved en **billetautomat**.
sentence.en: You can buy a ticket at a ticket machine.

en billetkontrollør.explanation: "En billetkontrollør" means "a ticket inspector". It is built from "billet" (ticket) and "kontrollør" (inspector).

sentence.da: En **billetkontrollør** tjekker billetterne i toget.
sentence.en: A ticket inspector checks the tickets on the train.

en bilnøgle.explanation: "En bilnøgle" means "a car key". The first part "bil" (car) is also at the start of other words, such as "en bilvask" (a car wash) and "en bilulykke" (a car accident).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke køre, fordi jeg har mistet min **bilnøgle**.
sentence.en: I can't drive because I lost my car key.

en bilulykke.explanation: "En bilulykke" means "a car accident". It is built from "bil" (car) and "ulykke" (accident). To say someone was in one, a very common phrase is "at komme ud for en bilulykke": "Han kom ud for en bilulykke i sidste uge" (He was in a car accident last week).

sentence.da: Der var en **bilulykke** på motorvejen i morges.
sentence.en: There was a car accident on the highway this morning.

en bilvask.explanation: "En bilvask" means "a car wash". It is built from "bil" (car) and "vask" (wash).

sentence.da: Bilen er meget beskidt, og vi skal finde en **bilvask**.
sentence.en: The car is very dirty, and we have to find a car wash.

en bindestreg.explanation: "En bindestreg" means "a hyphen". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "en streg" (a line), so literally it is a line that ties words together. The longer line is "en tankestreg" (a dash). To mark an extra remark in the middle of a sentence, use the dash: "Min bror – han bor i Aarhus – kommer i morgen" (My brother – he lives in Aarhus – is coming tomorrow).

sentence.da: Man skriver en **bindestreg** i ordet S-tog.
sentence.en: You write a hyphen in the word S-tog.

en biograf.explanation: "En biograf" means "a movie theater". To say you go to the movies, use "at gå i biografen": "Skal vi i biografen i aften?" (Shall we go to the movies tonight?) The short form "bio" also exists: "Vi går i bio" (We are going to the movies).

sentence.da: Vi ser en film i en stor **biograf**.
sentence.en: We watch a movie in a big movie theater.

en biografi.explanation: "En biografi" means "a biography". When a person writes about his or her own life, the word is "en selvbiografi" (an autobiography): "Hun har skrevet en selvbiografi" (She has written an autobiography).

sentence.da: En **biografi** om Niels Bohr fortæller om hans liv.
sentence.en: A biography of Niels Bohr tells about his life.

en biolog.explanation: "En biolog" means "a biologist". The ending "-log" is also in other words for experts, such as "en psykolog" (a psychologist) and "en geolog" (a geologist).

sentence.da: En **biolog** undersøger, hvordan dyr og planter lever sammen.
sentence.en: A biologist studies how animals and plants live together.

en birk.explanation: "En birk" means "a birch". The word is also joined with "et træ" (a tree) to make "et birketræ" (a birch tree).

sentence.da: Stammen på en **birk** er hvid med sorte pletter.
sentence.en: The trunk of a birch is white with black spots.

en bivirkning.explanation: "En bivirkning" means "a side effect". It is built from "bi-" (side) and "en virkning" (an effect). The same "bi-" is in "et bijob" (a side job).

sentence.da: Træthed er en almindelig **bivirkning** af den slags medicin.
sentence.en: Tiredness is a common side effect of that kind of medicine.

en bjergbestigning.explanation: "En bjergbestigning" means "a mountain climb". It is built from "et bjerg" (a mountain) and "en bestigning" (a climb), which comes from the verb "at bestige" (to climb up).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **bjergbestigning** stod vi på toppen.
sentence.en: After a long mountain climb we stood on top.

en bjørn.explanation: "En bjørn" means "a bear". To name a polar bear, join "is" (ice) and "bjørn": "en isbjørn" (a polar bear).

sentence.da: En **bjørn** er stor og kan løbe hurtigt.
sentence.en: A bear is big and can run fast.

en blanding.explanation: "En blanding" means "a mixture". A very common phrase is "en blanding af" (a mixture of): "Vi købte en blanding af nødder" (We bought a mixture of nuts).

sentence.da: Dejen er en **blanding** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: The dough is a mixture of flour and water.

en blanket.explanation: "En blanket" means "a form", as in a document with empty fields to fill in. To say you hand it in, use "at aflevere" (to hand in): "Du skal aflevere blanketten i morgen" (You have to hand in the form tomorrow).

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde denne **blanket**.
sentence.en: You have to fill in this form.

en ble.explanation: "En ble" means "a diaper". To say you change a diaper, use "at skifte" (to change): "Vil du skifte bleen?" (Will you change the diaper?)

sentence.da: Babyen har en våd **ble**.
sentence.en: The baby has a wet diaper.

en blender.explanation: "En blender" means "a blender". It is borrowed from the English word "blender".

sentence.da: Jeg laver en smoothie i min **blender**.
sentence.en: I make a smoothie in my blender.

en blikkenslager.explanation: "En blikkenslager" means "a plumber". It is built from "blik" (tin plate) and "at slå" (to hit), so literally it is someone who hits tin plate.

sentence.da: Vi ringer efter en **blikkenslager**, fordi hanen drypper.
sentence.en: We call a plumber because the tap is dripping.

en blodprop.explanation: "En blodprop" means "a blood clot". When the clot is in the head, say "en blodprop i hjernen" (a stroke). When it is in the heart, say "en blodprop i hjertet" (a heart attack).

sentence.da: En **blodprop** kan stoppe blodet i en åre.
sentence.en: A blood clot can stop the blood in a blood vessel.

en blodprøve.explanation: "En blodprøve" means "a blood test". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "en prøve" (a sample). To say a nurse takes your blood, you say you "have it taken": "Jeg skal have taget en blodprøve" (I have to have a blood test taken).

sentence.da: Lægen vil tage en **blodprøve**.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to take a blood sample.

en blodåre.explanation: "En blodåre" means "a blood vessel". It is built from "blod" (blood) and "en åre" (a vein). A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart is "en pulsåre" (an artery): "Lægen mærker på pulsåren i halsen" (The doctor feels the artery in the neck).

sentence.da: Når man skærer sig dybt, kan man ramme en **blodåre**.
sentence.en: When you cut yourself deeply, you can hit a blood vessel.

en blog.explanation: "En blog" means "a blog". To say someone writes a blog, use the verb "at blogge" (to blog): "Hun blogger om mad" (She blogs about food).

sentence.da: Min søster skriver en **blog** om sin hund.
sentence.en: My sister writes a blog about her dog.

en blok.explanation: "En blok" means "a notepad". The word also means "a block" of something solid, as in "en isblok" (a block of ice).

sentence.da: Man river et ark af en **blok**, når man har skrevet noget.
sentence.en: You tear a sheet off a notepad when you have written something.

en blomme.explanation: "En blomme" means "a plum". Do not mix it up with "en blomst" (a flower). To say you eat a plum, say "Jeg spiser en blomme" (I eat a plum). To say you pick a flower, say "Jeg plukker en blomst" (I pick a flower).

sentence.da: Denne **blomme** er sød og lilla.
sentence.en: This plum is sweet and purple.

en blomst.explanation: "En blomst" means "a flower". At the start of compound words it takes the form "blomster-", as in "en blomsterbutik" (a flower shop) and "en blomstervase" (a flower vase).

sentence.da: Hun plukker en smuk **blomst** i haven.
sentence.en: She picks a pretty flower in the garden.

en blomsterbuket.explanation: "En blomsterbuket" means "a bouquet". To say it in a shorter way, use "en buket" (a bouquet): "Hun fik en buket til sin fødselsdag" (She got a bouquet for her birthday).

sentence.da: Han kom med en **blomsterbuket** af røde roser til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: He came with a bouquet of red roses for my birthday.

en blomsterhandler.explanation: "En blomsterhandler" means "a florist". The word also means the shop: "Jeg går forbi blomsterhandleren" (I am walking past the florist's).

sentence.da: Jeg købte roser hos en **blomsterhandler** på hjørnet af gaden.
sentence.en: I bought roses from a florist on the corner of the street.

en blondine.explanation: "En blondine" means "a blonde". To describe a man or any other person, use the adjective "blond": "en blond mand" (a blond man).

sentence.da: Min søster er en **blondine**, og jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is a blonde, and I have dark hair.

en bluse.explanation: "En bluse" means "a blouse". Do not mix it up with "en skjorte" (a shirt): "Han har en skjorte på" (He is wearing a shirt).

sentence.da: Hun har en rød **bluse** på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a red blouse.

en blyant.explanation: "En blyant" means "a pencil". To say you sharpen a pencil, use "at spidse" (to sharpen): "Jeg spidser min blyant" (I am sharpening my pencil).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver med en **blyant**.
sentence.en: I write with a pencil.

en blæksprutte.explanation: "En blæksprutte" means "an octopus or squid". Danish uses one word for both animals. To say which one, add the number of arms: "en ottearmet blæksprutte" (an octopus) and "en tiarmet blæksprutte" (a squid). It is built from "blæk" (ink) and "at sprutte" (to squirt).

sentence.da: En **blæksprutte** sprøjter blæk ud i vandet, når den er bange.
sentence.en: An octopus squirts ink into the water when it is scared.

en blære.explanation: "En blære" means "a bladder". It also means "a blister" on the skin from a burn, as in "en brandblære" (a burn blister).

sentence.da: Nyrerne laver urin, som samles i en **blære**.
sentence.en: The kidneys make urine, which collects in a bladder.

en blødning.explanation: "En blødning" means "a bleeding". To say the blood stays inside the body, use "en indre blødning" (internal bleeding).

sentence.da: Tryk på såret, hvis du vil stoppe en **blødning**.
sentence.en: Press on the wound if you want to stop bleeding.

en bodega.explanation: "En bodega" means "a local bar". The word comes from Spanish "bodega" (a wine cellar or shop).

sentence.da: På vores lokale **bodega** kender alle hinanden og drikker billig øl.
sentence.en: At our local bodega everyone knows each other and drinks cheap beer.

en bodylotion.explanation: "En bodylotion" means "a body lotion". It is borrowed from English. To say you put it on all over, use "at smøre sig ind" (to rub oneself all over): "Jeg smører mig ind i bodylotion" (I rub body lotion all over myself).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **bodylotion** efter badet, fordi min hud er tør.
sentence.en: I use body lotion after the bath because my skin is dry.

en bog.explanation: "En bog" means "a book". To say you read a book, use "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser en bog hver aften" (I read a book every evening).

sentence.da: Man kan låne en **bog** på biblioteket.
sentence.en: You can borrow a book at the library.

en boghandel.explanation: "En boghandel" means "a bookstore". It is built from "bog" (book) and "handel" (trade). Do not mix it up with "et bibliotek" (a library), where you borrow books: "Jeg låner bogen på biblioteket" (I borrow the book at the library).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en roman i en **boghandel** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy a novel in a bookstore in town.

en boghandler.explanation: "En boghandler" means "a bookseller". The word also means the shop: "Jeg går forbi boghandleren" (I am walking past the bookstore).

sentence.da: En **boghandler** sælger bøger, men en bibliotekar låner dem ud.
sentence.en: A bookseller sells books, but a librarian lends them out.

en bogreol.explanation: "En bogreol" means "a bookcase". It is built from bog (book) and reol (open rack).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en større **bogreol** til alle bøgerne.
sentence.en: We need a bigger bookcase for all the books.

en bold.explanation: "En bold" means "a ball". To say you play with a ball, use "at spille bold" (to play ball): "Børnene spiller bold i haven" (The children are playing ball in the garden).

sentence.da: Man kan sparke og kaste en **bold**.
sentence.en: You can kick and throw a ball.

en bolig.explanation: "En bolig" means "a home", as in a place to live. To say someone has no permanent place to live, say "Han har ingen fast bolig" (He has no permanent home). Do not mix it up with "et hjem" (a home with a feeling of belonging): "Vi har et rart hjem" (We have a lovely home).

sentence.da: Vi leder efter en billig **bolig** i byen.
sentence.en: We are looking for a cheap home in the city.

en boligblok.explanation: "En boligblok" means "an apartment block". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en blok" (a block).

sentence.da: Der bor mange familier i en **boligblok**.
sentence.en: Many families live in an apartment block.

en boligforening.explanation: "En boligforening" means "a housing association". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en forening" (an association). In Denmark, "en almen boligforening" is a non-profit one that rents out homes.

sentence.da: En **boligforening** ejer mange lejligheder og har en lang venteliste.
sentence.en: A housing association owns many apartments and has a long waiting list.

en boligkarré.explanation: "En boligkarré" means "a city block". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "en karré" (a block of buildings).

sentence.da: Børnene leger i gården midt i en **boligkarré**.
sentence.en: The children play in the yard in the middle of a city block.

en bolle.explanation: "En bolle" means "a bun". It also means a meatball in the dish "boller i karry" (meatballs in curry): "Vi spiser boller i karry til middag" (We are eating meatballs in curry for dinner).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **bolle** med smør.
sentence.en: I eat a bun with butter.

en bombe.explanation: "En bombe" means "a bomb". To say someone threatens to use a bomb, use "en bombetrussel" (a bomb threat), built from "bombe" and "en trussel" (a threat): "Skolen fik en bombetrussel" (The school got a bomb threat).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **bombe** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The police found a bomb at the station.

en bon.explanation: "En bon" means "a receipt". To say you keep it, use "at gemme" (to keep): "Gem bonen, hvis du vil bytte varen" (Keep the receipt if you want to exchange the item).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler i kassen og får en **bon**.
sentence.en: I pay at the register and get a receipt.

en bonde.explanation: "En bonde" means "a farmer". A different meaning of the same word is "a pawn" in chess: "Jeg flytter en bonde" (I move a pawn).

sentence.da: En **bonde** står tidligt op og malker køerne.
sentence.en: A farmer gets up early and milks the cows.

en bonus.explanation: "En bonus" means "a bonus". To say you receive one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en bonus i december" (I got a bonus in December).

sentence.da: Firmaet giver os en **bonus**, når året er gået godt.
sentence.en: The company gives us a bonus when the year has gone well.

en bordplade.explanation: "En bordplade" means "a tabletop or countertop". Danish uses one word for both. It is built from "bord" (table) and "plade" (board).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en ny **bordplade** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We need a new countertop in the kitchen.

en boremaskine.explanation: "En boremaskine" means "a drill". It is built from "at bore" (to drill) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you drill a hole, say "Jeg borer et hul i væggen" (I am drilling a hole in the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **boremaskine** til at lave et hul.
sentence.en: I need a drill to make a hole.

en borg.explanation: "En borg" means "a castle". Do not mix it up with "et slot" (a palace). To say a count lives in a castle, say "Greven bor i en borg" (The count lives in a castle). To say a king lives in a palace, say "Kongen bor på et slot" (The king lives in a palace).

sentence.da: I middelalderen byggede man en **borg** for at forsvare sig.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages, people built a castle to defend themselves.

en borger.explanation: "En borger" means "a citizen". A municipality calls the people it serves "borgere": "Kommunen hjælper borgerne" (The municipality helps the citizens).

sentence.da: Hver **borger** over atten år må stemme ved valg.
sentence.en: Every citizen over eighteen may vote in elections.

en borgmester.explanation: "En borgmester" means "a mayor". To say someone is running for mayor, say "Hun stiller op som borgmester" (She is running for mayor). In Copenhagen the title is longer, "en overborgmester" (a lord mayor): "Københavns overborgmester holder tale" (Copenhagen's lord mayor gives a speech).

sentence.da: Byens **borgmester** holder en tale i dag.
sentence.en: The town's mayor gives a speech today.

en bosætning.explanation: "En bosætning" means "a settlement". It is built from the verb "at bosætte sig" (to settle down), so it also means the act of settling: "Familien overvejer bosætning i Jylland" (The family is considering settling in Jutland).

sentence.da: Ved åen opstod en **bosætning**, hvor folk byggede de første huse.
sentence.en: By the stream, a settlement arose where people built the first houses.

sentence.da: I en **botanisk have** kan man se planter fra hele verden.
sentence.en: In a botanical garden you can see plants from all over the world.

en bowlinghal.explanation: "En bowlinghal" means "a bowling alley". The ending "hal" (hall) is also in "en svømmehal" (an indoor swimming pool) and "en idrætshal" (a sports hall).

sentence.da: Der er en **bowlinghal** i byen, hvor man kan spille bowling.
sentence.en: There is a bowling alley in town where you can play bowling.

en bradepande.explanation: "En bradepande" means "a roasting pan". Do not mix it up with "en stegepande" (a frying pan). A roasting pan goes in the oven: "Kyllingen står i bradepanden" (The chicken is in the roasting pan). A frying pan goes on the stove: "Jeg steger æg i stegepanden" (I fry eggs in the frying pan).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger kartoflerne i en **bradepande** og sætter dem i ovnen.
sentence.en: I put the potatoes in a roasting pan and place them in the oven.

en branche.explanation: "En branche" means "an industry". To say what field you work in, add "-branchen": "Hun arbejder i it-branchen" (She works in the IT industry).

sentence.da: Min bror har arbejdet i den samme **branche** i ti år.
sentence.en: My brother has worked in the same line of business for ten years.

en brand.explanation: "En brand" means "a fire (blaze)". To say a fire starts, use "at bryde ud" (to break out): "Der brød en brand ud i nat" (A fire broke out last night). To talk about a small fire you light on purpose, say "et bål" (a campfire): "Vi tænder et bål" (We light a campfire).

sentence.da: Der var en stor **brand** i byen i nat.
sentence.en: There was a big fire in town last night.

en brandalarm.explanation: "En brandalarm" means "a fire alarm". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "alarm" (alarm). To say the alarm is sounding, use "at gå" (to go): "Brandalarmen går" (The fire alarm is going off).

sentence.da: En **brandalarm** ringer højt, når der er røg.
sentence.en: A fire alarm rings loudly when there is smoke.

en brandbil.explanation: "En brandbil" means "a fire truck". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "bil" (car). In Denmark you call 112 for a fire truck: "Ring til 112, hvis det brænder" (Call 112 if something is on fire).

sentence.da: Der er ild i huset, og en **brandbil** kommer.
sentence.en: There is a fire in the house, and a fire truck is coming.

en brandmand.explanation: "En brandmand" means "a firefighter". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "mand" (man). To say they put out a fire, use "at slukke" (to put out): "Brandmændene slukker branden" (The firefighters put out the fire).

sentence.da: En **brandmand** redder folk fra et brændende hus.
sentence.en: A firefighter rescues people from a burning house.
