en brandslukker.explanation: "En brandslukker" means "a fire extinguisher". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "at slukke" (to put out). The verb "at slukke" also means to switch off: "Jeg slukker lyset" (I turn off the light).

sentence.da: Brug en **brandslukker**, hvis det brænder.
sentence.en: Use a fire extinguisher if something is burning.

en brandstation.explanation: "En brandstation" means "a fire station". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "station", the same word as in "en togstation" (a train station).

sentence.da: Brandbilen holder foran den lille **brandstation**.
sentence.en: The fire truck is parked in front of the small fire station.

en brandtrappe.explanation: "En brandtrappe" means "a fire escape". It is built from "brand" (fire) and "en trappe" (a staircase). To say you left a building this way, say "Vi gik ned ad brandtrappen" (We went down the fire escape).

sentence.da: En **brandtrappe** bruges, når den almindelige trappe er spærret af ild.
sentence.en: A fire escape is used when the ordinary stairs are blocked by fire.

en bredde.explanation: "En bredde" means "a width". It comes from the adjective "bred" (wide). When you name length and width together, length comes first: "længde og bredde" (length and width).

sentence.da: Vinduet har en **bredde** på to meter.
sentence.en: The window has a width of two meters.

en bregne.explanation: "En bregne" means "a fern". Do not mix it up with "et mos" (a moss). A fern grows in the shade: "Bregnen trives i skyggen" (The fern thrives in the shade). Moss grows on stone: "Der vokser mos på stenen" (Moss grows on the stone).

sentence.da: I skoven vokser der en **bregne** med lange, fine blade.
sentence.en: In the forest there grows a fern with long, fine leaves.

en bremse.explanation: "En bremse" means "a brake". The verb is "at bremse" (to brake): "Jeg bremser for rødt lys" (I brake for a red light). A different meaning of the same word is "a horsefly", an insect: "En bremse stak mig" (A horsefly stung me).

sentence.da: En **bremse** får bilen til at stoppe.
sentence.en: A brake makes the car stop.

en brevkasse.explanation: "En brevkasse" means "a mailbox". It also means "an advice column" in a newspaper or magazine: "Brevkassen i bladet svarer på spørgsmål om kærlighed" (The advice column in the magazine answers questions about love).

sentence.da: Læserne sender deres spørgsmål til avisens **brevkasse** og får råd.
sentence.en: The readers send their questions to the paper's advice column and get advice.

en brevsprække.explanation: "En brevsprække" means "a mail slot". It is built from "brev" (letter) and "sprække" (slit). The word "sprække" also means a crack, as in "en sprække i muren" (a crack in the wall).

sentence.da: Posten falder på gulvet gennem en **brevsprække**.
sentence.en: The mail falls onto the floor through a mail slot.

en brik.explanation: "En brik" means "a piece", as in a piece you move in a board game. To name a tile in Scrabble, use "en scrabblebrik" (a Scrabble tile).

sentence.da: Spilleren flytter en **brik** hen over brættet.
sentence.en: The player moves a piece across the board.

en brise.explanation: "En brise" means "a breeze". A very common phrase is "en frisk brise" (a fresh breeze): "Der er en frisk brise i dag" (There is a fresh breeze today).

sentence.da: Der kommer en let **brise** ind fra havet.
sentence.en: A light breeze comes in from the sea.

en brite.explanation: "En brite" means "a Brit". It comes from "Storbritannien" (Great Britain). Danish nationality words are not capitalized, so "brite" starts with a lowercase b: "Han er brite" (He is a Brit).

sentence.da: En **brite** kan komme fra England, Skotland eller Wales.
sentence.en: A Brit can come from England, Scotland or Wales.

sentence.da: Vi går over en **bro** over vandet.
sentence.en: We walk over a bridge over the water.

en brochure.explanation: "En brochure" means "a brochure". It is borrowed from French.

sentence.da: Hotellet sendte mig en **brochure** med mange billeder.
sentence.en: The hotel sent me a brochure with many pictures.

en bror.explanation: "En bror" means "a brother". Danish has separate words for older and younger: "storebror" (big brother) and "lillebror" (little brother), as in "Min lillebror er fem år" (My little brother is five years old).

sentence.da: Min **bror** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My brother and I have the same mother.

en brownie.explanation: "En brownie" means "a brownie". It is borrowed from English. To say you want one with ice cream, say "en brownie med is" (a brownie with ice cream): "Jeg vil gerne have en brownie med is" (I would like a brownie with ice cream).

sentence.da: En **brownie** er en kage med meget chokolade.
sentence.en: A brownie is a cake with a lot of chocolate.

en browser.explanation: "En browser" means "a browser". It is borrowed from English. To say you update it, use "at opdatere" (to update): "Prøv at opdatere din browser" (Try updating your browser).

sentence.da: Jeg åbner min **browser** og søger efter opskriften.
sentence.en: I open my browser and search for the recipe.

en brudekjole.explanation: "En brudekjole" means "a wedding dress". It is built from "en brud" (a bride) and "en kjole" (a dress). To say someone is trying them on, say "Hun prøver brudekjoler i dag" (She is trying on wedding dresses today).

sentence.da: Til brylluppet har bruden en hvid **brudekjole** på.
sentence.en: At the wedding, the bride is wearing a white wedding dress.

en brudepige.explanation: "En brudepige" means "a bridesmaid". It is built from "en brud" (a bride) and "en pige" (a girl).

sentence.da: Min søster skal være **brudepige** til brylluppet.
sentence.en: My sister is going to be a bridesmaid at the wedding.

en brudgom.explanation: "En brudgom" means "a groom". To talk about the bride and groom together, use "et brudepar" (a bridal couple): "Brudeparret danser først" (The bridal couple dance first).

sentence.da: Han er en glad **brudgom** på sin bryllupsdag.
sentence.en: He is a happy groom on his wedding day.

en bruger.explanation: "En bruger" means "a user". It is built from "at bruge" (to use). The verb also means to spend: "Jeg bruger for mange penge" (I spend too much money).

sentence.da: Hver **bruger** har sin egen adgangskode.
sentence.en: Every user has their own password.

en brugsanvisning.explanation: "En brugsanvisning" means "a user manual". It is built from "brug" (use) and "anvisning" (instruction). To tell someone to read it, say "Læs brugsanvisningen, før du starter maskinen" (Read the manual before you start the machine).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **brugsanvisning**, fordi maskinen er ny.
sentence.en: I am reading a user manual because the machine is new.

en brunch.explanation: "En brunch" means "a brunch". It is borrowed from English. Do not mix it up with "morgenmad" (breakfast): "Jeg spiser morgenmad klokken syv" (I eat breakfast at seven o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **brunch** sent om søndagen.
sentence.en: We eat brunch late on Sundays.

en brunkage.explanation: "En brunkage" means "a Danish spice cookie". It is built from "brun" (brown) and "en kage" (a cake). In Denmark it is a Christmas cookie: "Vi bager brunkager til jul" (We bake brunkager for Christmas).

sentence.da: En **brunkage** smager af kanel, nelliker og sirup.
sentence.en: A brunkage tastes of cinnamon, cloves and syrup.

en brunsviger.explanation: "En brunsviger" means "a Funen brown-sugar cake". It comes from the island of Funen (Fyn). The first part "brun" (brown) is also in "en brunkage" (a Danish spice cookie).

sentence.da: En **brunsviger** er en blød gærkage med sukker og smør på toppen.
sentence.en: A brunsviger is a soft yeast cake with sugar and butter on top.

en bruser.explanation: "En bruser" means "a shower". To say you take a shower, use "et brusebad" (a shower bath): "Jeg tager et brusebad" (I take a shower).

sentence.da: Der er en ny **bruser** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: There is a new shower in the bathroom.

en bryllupsdag.explanation: "En bryllupsdag" means "a wedding anniversary". It also means the day of the wedding itself, as in "Han er en glad brudgom på sin bryllupsdag" (He is a happy groom on his wedding day).

sentence.da: I dag er det vores **bryllupsdag**, og vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: Today is our wedding anniversary, and we are eating out.

en bryllupsrejse.explanation: "En bryllupsrejse" means "a honeymoon". It is built from "bryllup" (wedding) and "rejse" (journey).

sentence.da: Vi vil på **bryllupsrejse** til Italien i maj.
sentence.en: We want to go on our honeymoon to Italy in May.

en brændenælde.explanation: "En brændenælde" means "a stinging nettle". It is built from "at brænde" (to burn) and "en nælde" (a nettle).

sentence.da: Hvis du rører ved en **brændenælde**, svier huden.
sentence.en: If you touch a stinging nettle, the skin stings.

en brødkniv.explanation: "En brødkniv" means "a bread knife". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "kniv" (knife).

sentence.da: Han skærer det friske brød med en **brødkniv**.
sentence.en: He cuts the fresh bread with a bread knife.

en brødkurv.explanation: "En brødkurv" means "a bread basket". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "kurv" (basket).

sentence.da: Vi lægger brødet i en **brødkurv**.
sentence.en: We put the bread in a bread basket.

en brødrister.explanation: "En brødrister" means "a toaster". It is built from "brød" (bread) and "at riste" (to toast).

sentence.da: En **brødrister** gør brødet varmt og sprødt.
sentence.en: A toaster makes the bread warm and crispy.

en brøk.explanation: "En brøk" means "a fraction". To name the parts of a fraction, say "en tæller" (a numerator) for the top number and "en nævner" (a denominator) for the bottom number.

sentence.da: En fjerdedel af en pizza er en **brøk**.
sentence.en: A quarter of a pizza is a fraction.

en brønd.explanation: "En brønd" means "a well". To say people dig one, use "at grave" (to dig): "De graver en brønd i haven" (They are digging a well in the garden). The word is also used for oil, as in "en oliebrønd" (an oil well).

sentence.da: Vandet i landsbyen kommer op fra en dyb **brønd**.
sentence.en: The water in the village comes up from a deep well.

en buffet.explanation: "En buffet" means "a buffet". To say there is a buffet at a meal, the word needs no "en": "Der er buffet til frokost" (There is a buffet for lunch).

sentence.da: Vi tager selv mad fra den store **buffet**.
sentence.en: We take food ourselves from the big buffet.

en bugt.explanation: "En bugt" means "a bay". It has a second meaning, "a bend", as in a river. To say there is a bend in a river, use the same word: "en bugt i floden" (a bend in the river).

sentence.da: En **bugt** er et sted, hvor havet går ind i landet.
sentence.en: A bay is a place where the sea goes into the land.

en bule.explanation: "En bule" means "a dent". It also means "a bump" on the body. To say you have a bump on your forehead, use the same word: "en bule i panden" (a bump on the forehead).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **bule** i bildøren efter ulykken.
sentence.en: There is a big dent in the car door after the accident.

en bums.explanation: "En bums" means "a pimple". To say where a pimple is, add the place: "en bums i panden" (a pimple on the forehead).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **bums** på næsen, og den gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: I got a pimple on my nose, and it hurt.

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", as in the lowest part of something. To say something lies at the lowest point of the sea, say: "på bunden af havet" (on the bottom of the sea). The word is also in "en tærtebund" (a pie base).

sentence.da: En kop har en flad **bund**.
sentence.en: A cup has a flat bottom.

en bundlinje.explanation: "En bundlinje" means "a bottom line". It is built from "bund" (bottom) and "en linje" (a line).

sentence.da: Firmaets **bundlinje** viser, om det tjente penge i år.
sentence.en: The company's bottom line shows whether it made money this year.

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile". To talk about a pile of clothes, say: "en bunke tøj" (a pile of clothes). To say someone has a large amount of money, use the same word: "en bunke penge" (a large amount of money).

sentence.da: En **bunke** er rodet, men en stak er pæn.
sentence.en: A pile is messy, but a stack is neat.

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger". To name a burger without meat, put the main ingredient first: "en vegetarburger" (a vegetarian burger).

sentence.da: En **burger** er kød mellem to stykker brød.
sentence.en: A burger is meat between two pieces of bread.

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you travel by bus, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager bussen" (I take the bus).

sentence.da: En **bus** har plads til mange mennesker.
sentence.en: A bus has room for many people.

en busbillet.explanation: "En busbillet" means "a bus ticket". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en billet" (a ticket); "billet" is also in "en biografbillet" (a cinema ticket) and "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **busbillet** i bussen.
sentence.en: You need a bus ticket on the bus.

en buschauffør.explanation: "En buschauffør" means "a bus driver". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en chauffør" (a driver); "chauffør" is also in "en taxachauffør" (a taxi driver) and "en lastbilchauffør" (a truck driver).

sentence.da: En **buschauffør** kører bussen hele dagen.
sentence.en: A bus driver drives the bus all day.

en busk.explanation: "En busk" means "a bush". To name a bush by the flower it carries, put the flower first: "en rosenbusk" (a rose bush).

sentence.da: Bærrene vokser på en **busk**.
sentence.en: The berries grow on a bush.

en butik.explanation: "En butik" means "a shop". To name a shop by what it sells, put the goods first: "en blomsterbutik" (a flower shop).

sentence.da: Jeg køber sko i en **butik** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy shoes in a shop in town.

en butiksansat.explanation: "En butiksansat" means "a store employee". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "ansat" (employed).

sentence.da: Som **butiksansat** hjælper hun kunderne og fylder hylderne op.
sentence.en: As a store employee, she helps the customers and fills up the shelves.

en butiksindehaver.explanation: "En butiksindehaver" means "a shop owner". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en indehaver" (a holder). The part "indehaver" is also used for the holder of a card: "indehaveren af kortet" (the holder of the card).

sentence.da: Han er **butiksindehaver** og åbner selv butikken hver morgen.
sentence.en: He is a shop owner and opens the shop himself every morning.

en butikskæde.explanation: "En butikskæde" means "a store chain". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en kæde" (a chain); "kæde" is also in "en hotelkæde" (a hotel chain) and "en cykelkæde" (a bicycle chain).

sentence.da: Den nye **butikskæde** har nu over tyve butikker i landet.
sentence.en: The new store chain now has over twenty shops in the country.

en butterfly.explanation: "En butterfly" means "a bow tie". To talk about the insect, use "en sommerfugl" (a butterfly): "En sommerfugl sidder på blomsten" (A butterfly is sitting on the flower).

sentence.da: Til festen havde han smoking og **butterfly** på.
sentence.en: At the party, he wore a tuxedo and a bow tie.

en by.explanation: "En by" means "a town". The same word also means "a city". To call a big place a city, say: "København er en by" (Copenhagen is a city). To say you are in town, use "i byen": "Jeg er i byen" (I am in town).

sentence.da: Der er mange huse i en **by**.
sentence.en: There are many houses in a town.

en bydel.explanation: "En bydel" means "a district". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en del" (a part); "del" is also in "en landsdel" (a region of a country) and "en verdensdel" (a continent).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en rolig **bydel** nær havnen.
sentence.en: We live in a quiet part of town near the harbor.

en byfest.explanation: "En byfest" means "a town festival". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en fest" (a party); "fest" is also in "en fødselsdagsfest" (a birthday party).

sentence.da: Hver sommer holder byen en stor **byfest** på torvet.
sentence.en: Every summer, the town holds a big town festival in the square.

en byge.explanation: "En byge" means "a shower", as in a short spell of rain. For the shower you wash in, use "et brusebad": "Jeg tager et brusebad" (I take a shower).

sentence.da: Der kom en kraftig **byge**, og vi blev våde.
sentence.en: A heavy shower came and we got wet.

en byggeplads.explanation: "En byggeplads" means "a construction site". It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en plads" (a place); "plads" is also in "en parkeringsplads" (a parking lot) and "en legeplads" (a playground).

sentence.da: De bygger et nyt hus på en **byggeplads**.
sentence.en: They are building a new house on a construction site.

en bygherre.explanation: "En bygherre" means "a developer", as in the person or company that orders a building. It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en herre" (a lord).

sentence.da: En **bygherre** bestiller huset og betaler for det.
sentence.en: A developer orders the house and pays for it.

en byrde.explanation: "En byrde" means "a burden". To say someone is carrying a burden, use "at bære på" (to carry): "Han bærer på en stor byrde" (He is carrying a big burden).

sentence.da: Det er en tung **byrde**, når man skylder mange penge.
sentence.en: It is a heavy burden when you owe a lot of money.

en bytteseddel.explanation: "En bytteseddel" means "a gift receipt". It is built from "at bytte" (to swap) and "en seddel" (a slip); "seddel" is also in "en pengeseddel" (a banknote).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en **bytteseddel** i pakken, hvis hun vil bytte den.
sentence.en: I put a gift receipt in the package in case she wants to swap it.

en båd.explanation: "En båd" means "a boat". To talk about a large ship, use "et skib" (a ship): "Skibet sejler til Norge" (The ship sails to Norway).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **båd** til øen.
sentence.en: We are taking a boat to the island.

en bæk.explanation: "En bæk" means "a brook". To talk about a bigger stream, use "en å" (a small river): "Åen løber gennem byen" (The river runs through the town).

sentence.da: Vandet løber i en lille **bæk** gennem engen.
sentence.en: The water runs in a little brook through the meadow.

en bæltetaske.explanation: "En bæltetaske" means "a fanny pack". It is built from "et bælte" (a belt) and "en taske" (a bag); "taske" is also in "en skoletaske" (a school bag) and "en indkøbstaske" (a shopping bag).

sentence.da: Hun bærer en lille **bæltetaske** om livet.
sentence.en: She carries a small fanny pack around her waist.

en bænk.explanation: "En bænk" means "a bench". To name a bench by its place, put the place first: "en parkbænk" (a park bench).

sentence.da: Vi sætter os på en **bænk** og hviler.
sentence.en: We sit down on a bench and rest.

en bærbar computer.explanation: "En bærbar computer" means "a laptop". "Bærbar" is built from "at bære" (to carry) and "-bar" (-able). To say "the laptop", add an "e" to "bærbar": "den bærbare computer".

sentence.da: Jeg har en **bærbar computer** i min taske.
sentence.en: I have a laptop in my bag.

en bæver.explanation: "En bæver" means "a beaver". To name the dam a beaver builds, say: "en bæverdæmning" (a beaver dam).

sentence.da: En **bæver** fælder træer og bygger en dæmning i åen.
sentence.en: A beaver fells trees and builds a dam in the stream.

en bøde.explanation: "En bøde" means "a fine", as in a penalty for breaking a rule. To say you have to pay one, use "at betale" (to pay): "Jeg skal betale en bøde" (I have to pay a fine). The word is also in "en parkeringsbøde" (a parking fine).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **bøde**, fordi jeg parkerede forkert.
sentence.en: I got a fine because I parked in the wrong place.

en bøf.explanation: "En bøf" means "a steak". For a patty of ground meat, use "en hakkebøf" (a ground beef patty): "Jeg spiser en hakkebøf med løg" (I am eating a ground beef patty with onions).

sentence.da: Han steger en **bøf** på panden.
sentence.en: He is frying a steak in the pan.

en bøg.explanation: "En bøg" means "a beech". The beech is the national tree of Denmark.

sentence.da: En **bøg** er et stort træ med glat, grå bark.
sentence.en: A beech is a big tree with smooth, gray bark.

en bøjle.explanation: "En bøjle" means "a hanger". The same word is in "en tandbøjle" (braces for teeth).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger skjorten på en **bøjle**.
sentence.en: I hang the shirt on a hanger.

en bøjning.explanation: "En bøjning" means "an inflection", as in grammar. To show how a verb changes, take "at spise" (to eat): "spiser", "spiste" and "spist" (eats, ate, eaten) are its inflections. To talk about a physical bend, use "en knæbøjning" (a knee bend), which comes from "at bøje" (to bend).

sentence.da: Det er svært at lære **bøjning** af alle de uregelmæssige verber.
sentence.en: It is hard to learn the inflection of all the irregular verbs.

en bølge.explanation: "En bølge" means "a wave", as in the sea. The word is also in "en hedebølge" (a heat wave) and "en kuldebølge" (a cold wave).

sentence.da: En stor **bølge** ramte båden.
sentence.en: A big wave hit the boat.

en bølgelængde.explanation: "En bølgelængde" means "a wavelength". It is built from "en bølge" (a wave) and "en længde" (a length).

sentence.da: Rødt lys har en længere **bølgelængde** end blåt lys.
sentence.en: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue light.

en bøn.explanation: "En bøn" means "a prayer". It also means "a plea". To say you ask for help with strong feeling, use "en bøn om hjælp" (a plea for help). The plural "bønner" is also the plural of "en bønne" (a bean): "Jeg spiser bønner" (I am eating beans).

sentence.da: Hun sagde en **bøn**, før hun faldt i søvn.
sentence.en: She said a prayer before she fell asleep.

en børnehave.explanation: "En børnehave" means "a kindergarten". In Denmark it is for children from about three to six, before school starts. It is built from "børn" (children) and "en have" (a garden).

sentence.da: Min datter er fire og går i **børnehave**.
sentence.en: My daughter is four and goes to kindergarten.

en børnelæge.explanation: "En børnelæge" means "a pediatrician". It is built from "børn" (children) and "en læge" (a doctor); "læge" is also in "en dyrlæge" (a vet).

sentence.da: Når et barn er sygt, kan man gå til en **børnelæge**.
sentence.en: When a child is sick, you can go to a pediatrician.

en børnemenu.explanation: "En børnemenu" means "a kids' menu". It is built from "børn" (children) and "en menu" (a menu); "menu" is also in "en frokostmenu" (a lunch menu).

sentence.da: Har I en **børnemenu** til mit barn?
sentence.en: Do you have a kids' menu for my child?

en børste.explanation: "En børste" means "a brush". The same word is the base of the verb "at børste" (to brush): "Jeg børster tænder" (I brush my teeth).

sentence.da: Jeg har en blød **børste** til mit hår.
sentence.en: I have a soft brush for my hair.

et bad.explanation: "Et bad" means "a bath or shower". To say you swim in the sea or a lake, use the verb "at bade" (to bathe): "Vi bader i havet" (We are swimming in the sea).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **bad** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I take a shower every morning.

et badekar.explanation: "Et badekar" means "a bathtub". It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et kar" (a tub).

sentence.da: Hun lægger sig i et **badekar** og slapper af.
sentence.en: She lies down in a bathtub and relaxes.

et badested.explanation: "Et badested" means "a swimming spot". It also means "a seaside resort". To say a place is a seaside resort, use the same word: "Blokhus er et badested" (Blokhus is a seaside resort). It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et sted" (a place).

sentence.da: Vi kører til et **badested**, hvor vandet er rent og roligt.
sentence.en: We drive to a swimming spot where the water is clean and calm.

et badeværelse.explanation: "Et badeværelse" means "a bathroom". It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et værelse" (a room). To ask where a public toilet is, use "toilettet" (the toilet): "Hvor er toilettet?" (Where is the toilet?).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **badeværelse** med bad.
sentence.en: We have a small bathroom with a shower.

et bagagebånd.explanation: "Et bagagebånd" means "a baggage carousel". It is built from "bagage" (baggage) and "et bånd" (a belt); "bånd" is also in "et målebånd" (a measuring tape) and "et løbebånd" (a treadmill).

sentence.da: Vi venter ved **bagagebånd** nummer to.
sentence.en: We are waiting at baggage carousel number two.

et bagagerum.explanation: "Et bagagerum" means "a trunk", as in the back of a car. It is built from "bagage" (luggage) and "et rum" (a room), so literally it is a "luggage room".

sentence.da: Vores nye bil har et stort **bagagerum**.
sentence.en: Our new car has a big trunk.

et bageri.explanation: "Et bageri" means "a bakery". It comes from the verb "at bage" (to bake). At a bakery in Denmark you can buy "wienerbrød" (literally, Vienna bread), which English speakers call a Danish pastry.

sentence.da: Jeg køber brød og kager i et **bageri**.
sentence.en: I buy bread and cakes in a bakery.

et baghold.explanation: "Et baghold" means "an ambush". To say someone waits hidden to attack, use "at ligge i baghold" (to lie in ambush): "Soldaterne lå i baghold" (The soldiers lay in ambush).

sentence.da: Fjenden blev lokket ind i et **baghold** i skoven.
sentence.en: The enemy was lured into an ambush in the forest.

et bal.explanation: "Et bal" means "a ball", as in a formal dance. For the round ball you kick, use "en bold" (a ball): "Han sparker til bolden" (He kicks the ball).

sentence.da: Til et **bal** danser gæsterne hele aftenen.
sentence.en: At a ball, the guests dance all evening.

et band.explanation: "Et band" means "a band". For a ribbon or tape, use "et bånd" (a ribbon): "Hun binder et bånd i håret" (She ties a ribbon in her hair). The plural is "bands", with an s as in English.

sentence.da: Vores **band** spiller til en fest i morgen.
sentence.en: Our band is playing at a party tomorrow.

et barn.explanation: "Et barn" means "a child". To talk about more than one, use the irregular plural "børn" (children): "Vi har to børn" (We have two children).

sentence.da: Hun har et lille **barn** hjemme.
sentence.en: She has a small child at home.

et barnebarn.explanation: "Et barnebarn" means "a grandchild". It is built from "et barn" (a child) twice, so literally it is a "child's child". To talk about more than one, use the irregular plural "børnebørn" (grandchildren): "Jeg har fire børnebørn" (I have four grandchildren).

sentence.da: Min datters barn er mit **barnebarn**.
sentence.en: My daughter's child is my grandchild.

et batteri.explanation: "Et batteri" means "a battery". To say a battery is dead, use "fladt" (literally, flat): "Batteriet er fladt" (The battery is dead).

sentence.da: Mit **batteri** er næsten tomt.
sentence.en: My battery is almost empty.

et bed.explanation: "Et bed" means "a flower bed". For a bed to sleep in, use "en seng" (a bed): "Jeg sover i min seng" (I sleep in my bed).

sentence.da: Der er mange røde blomster i mit **bed**.
sentence.en: There are many red flowers in my flower bed.

et bedrag.explanation: "Et bedrag" means "a deception". For the crime of cheating someone out of money, use "et bedrageri" (a fraud): "Politiet efterforsker et bedrageri" (The police are investigating a fraud). The word is also in "selvbedrag" (self-deception).

sentence.da: Det var et **bedrag**, da han solgte falske billetter.
sentence.en: It was a deception when he sold fake tickets.

et bedrageri.explanation: "Et bedrageri" means "a fraud". It comes from the verb "at bedrage" (to deceive).

sentence.da: Han blev dømt for **bedrageri**, fordi han snød mange ældre for penge.
sentence.en: He was convicted of fraud because he cheated many elderly people out of money.

et begreb.explanation: "Et begreb" means "a concept". To say you have no idea about something, use "ikke have begreb om" (to have no idea about): "Jeg har ikke begreb om, hvad det koster" (I have no idea what it costs).

sentence.da: Tyngdekraft er et **begreb** inden for fysik.
sentence.en: Gravity is a concept within physics.

et behov.explanation: "Et behov" means "a need". To say you need something, use "at have behov for" (to have a need for): "Jeg har behov for hvile" (I need rest).

sentence.da: Der er et stort **behov** for lærere.
sentence.en: There is a great need for teachers.

et belæg.explanation: "Et belæg" means "a basis or evidence". To ask someone to back up a claim, say: "Har du belæg for det?" (Do you have grounds for that?).

sentence.da: Der er intet **belæg** for hans påstand.
sentence.en: There is no evidence for his claim.

et beløb.explanation: "Et beløb" means "an amount of money". For an amount of other things, use "en mængde" (a quantity): "en stor mængde vand" (a large quantity of water).

sentence.da: Det samlede **beløb** er tusind kroner.
sentence.en: The total amount is a thousand kroner.

et ben.explanation: "Et ben" means "a leg or bone". Danes say "benet" (the leg) where English says "his leg": "Han har brækket benet" (He has broken his leg). To talk about the bone of the upper leg, use "et lårben" (a thigh bone).

sentence.da: En hund har fire **ben**.
sentence.en: A dog has four legs.

et besøg.explanation: "Et besøg" means "a visit". To say you are visiting someone, use "på besøg": "Jeg er på besøg hos min mor" (I am visiting my mother).

sentence.da: Tak for dit **besøg** i går.
sentence.en: Thank you for your visit yesterday.

et betalingskort.explanation: "Et betalingskort" means "a payment card". It is built from "en betaling" (a payment) and "et kort" (a card). A well-known Danish payment card is the "Dankort".

sentence.da: Jeg betaler med mit **betalingskort**.
sentence.en: I pay with my payment card.

et bevis.explanation: "Et bevis" means "a proof". It also means "evidence". To say the police have no evidence, say: "Politiet har ingen beviser" (The police have no evidence).

sentence.da: Jeg tror dig ikke uden **bevis**.
sentence.en: I do not believe you without proof.

et bibliotek.explanation: "Et bibliotek" means "a library". To say you are at the library, use "på biblioteket": "Jeg er på biblioteket" (I am at the library).

sentence.da: På et **bibliotek** kan man låne bøger gratis.
sentence.en: At a library you can borrow books for free.

et bibliotekskort.explanation: "Et bibliotekskort" means "a library card". It is built from "et bibliotek" (a library) and "et kort" (a card). To say a map, use the same word "kort": "Jeg har et kort over byen" (I have a map of the city).

sentence.da: Jeg viser mit **bibliotekskort** og låner tre bøger.
sentence.en: I show my library card and borrow three books.

et bidrag.explanation: "Et bidrag" means "a contribution". The word is also in "børnebidrag" (child support), a regular payment.

sentence.da: Hvert **bidrag** til indsamlingen hjælper børnene.
sentence.en: Every contribution to the fundraiser helps the children.

et billede.explanation: "Et billede" means "a picture". To say you take a picture, use "at tage et billede": "Må jeg tage et billede?" (May I take a picture?). For a picture taken with a camera, you can also use "et foto" (a photo): "Jeg tog et foto af huset" (I took a photo of the house).

sentence.da: Hun maler et **billede** af havet.
sentence.en: She paints a picture of the sea.

et bind.explanation: "Et bind" means "a volume", as in one book of a set. It comes from the verb "at binde" (to tie). To say which one, put the number after it: "bind 2" (volume 2).

sentence.da: Det første **bind** af værket handler om krigen.
sentence.en: The first volume of the work is about the war.

et bindeord.explanation: "Et bindeord" means "a conjunction". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "et ord" (a word). To join two parts of a sentence, use one such as "og" (and): "Jeg spiser og drikker" (I eat and drink).

sentence.da: Ordet fordi er et **bindeord**, som forbinder to sætninger.
sentence.en: The word fordi (because) is a conjunction that connects two sentences.

et biord.explanation: "Et biord" means "an adverb". It is built from "bi-" (side) and "et ord" (a word), so literally it is a "side word". To say how something is done, use one such as "hurtigt" (quickly): "Han løber hurtigt" (He runs quickly).

sentence.da: Ordet nu er et **biord**, fordi det fortæller, hvornår noget sker.
sentence.en: The word nu (now) is an adverb because it tells when something happens.

et bistade.explanation: "Et bistade" means "a beehive". Another word for it is "en bikube" (a beehive): "Han passer sin bikube" (He looks after his beehive).

sentence.da: Der bor mange tusinde bier i et **bistade**.
sentence.en: Many thousands of bees live in a beehive.

et bjerg.explanation: "Et bjerg" means "a mountain". For a lower rise, use "en bakke" (a hill): "Vi cykler op ad en bakke" (We cycle up a hill).

sentence.da: Vi går op på et stort **bjerg**.
sentence.en: We walk up a big mountain.

et blad.explanation: "Et blad" means "a magazine or a leaf". To talk about the leaf of a tree, say: "Træet har grønne blade" (The tree has green leaves). The word is also in "et dagblad" (a daily newspaper).

sentence.da: Jeg køber et **blad** med opskrifter og billeder.
sentence.en: I buy a magazine with recipes and pictures.

et blik.explanation: "Et blik" means "a look". To say someone glanced at something, use "at kaste et blik på" (to cast a glance at): "Han kastede et blik på uret" (He glanced at the clock).

sentence.da: Hun så på mig med et trist **blik**.
sentence.en: She looked at me with a sad look.

et blinklys.explanation: "Et blinklys" means "a turn signal". It is built from "blink" (blink) and "et lys" (a light). To say you signal, use "at blinke" (to blink): "Jeg blinker til højre" (I signal right).

sentence.da: Husk at bruge **blinklys**, når du drejer.
sentence.en: Remember to use your turn signal when you turn.

et blomsterbed.explanation: "Et blomsterbed" means "a flower bed". It is built from "en blomst" (a flower) and "et bed" (a bed). To talk about a bed of vegetables, use "et bed" alone: "et bed med gulerødder" (a bed of carrots).

sentence.da: Tulipanerne vokser i et **blomsterbed** foran huset.
sentence.en: The tulips grow in a flower bed in front of the house.

et blåbær.explanation: "Et blåbær" means "a blueberry". It is built from "blå" (blue) and "et bær" (a berry); "blå" is also in "en blåhval" (a blue whale).

sentence.da: **Blåbær** er små, runde og blå.
sentence.en: Blueberries are small, round and blue.

et blåt mærke.explanation: "Et blåt mærke" means "a bruise". Literally, it is "a blue mark". After "et" the word is "blåt", but after "det" it is "blå": "det blå mærke" (the bruise).

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **blåt mærke** på benet, da jeg faldt.
sentence.en: I got a bruise on my leg when I fell.

et boardingpas.explanation: "Et boardingpas" means "a boarding pass". For the book you carry to travel abroad, use "et pas" (a passport): "Jeg viser mit pas" (I show my passport).

sentence.da: Jeg viser mit **boardingpas** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: I show my boarding pass at the airport.

et bogstav.explanation: "Et bogstav" means "a letter (of the alphabet)". For a letter you send in the post, use "et brev" (a letter): "Jeg skriver et brev" (I am writing a letter).

sentence.da: Hvilket **bogstav** kommer efter B?
sentence.en: Which letter comes after B?

et boligmarked.explanation: "Et boligmarked" means "a housing market". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "et marked" (a market). To say you want to buy a home, use "at købe bolig" (to buy a home): "Vi vil købe bolig" (We want to buy a home).

sentence.da: På et **boligmarked** stiger priserne, når mange vil købe.
sentence.en: In a housing market, prices rise when many people want to buy.

et bonuskort.explanation: "Et bonuskort" means "a loyalty card". It is built from "bonus" (a reward) and "et kort" (a card).

sentence.da: Med mit **bonuskort** får jeg point, hver gang jeg handler.
sentence.en: With my loyalty card, I get points every time I shop.

et bord.explanation: "Et bord" means "a table". To ask for a table in a restaurant, say: "Et bord til to, tak" (A table for two, please). For a desk, use "et skrivebord" (literally, a writing table): "Jeg sidder ved mit skrivebord" (I am sitting at my desk).

sentence.da: Vi spiser ved et **bord** med fire stole.
sentence.en: We eat at a table with four chairs.

et brag.explanation: "Et brag" means "a bang or crash". To say something ended with a big finish, use "med et brag" (with a bang): "Festen sluttede med et brag" (The party ended with a bang).

sentence.da: Døren lukkede med et stort **brag**.
sentence.en: The door closed with a big bang.

et brandvæsen.explanation: "Et brandvæsen" means "a fire department". It is built from "en brand" (a fire) and "et væsen" (a service); "væsen" is also in "sundhedsvæsenet" (the health service). In Denmark, you call 112 for the fire department.

sentence.da: Et **brandvæsen** slukker brande og redder folk ud af biler.
sentence.en: A fire department puts out fires and rescues people from cars.

et brev.explanation: "Et brev" means "a letter". For an email, use "en mail" (an email): "Jeg sender en mail" (I am sending an email).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter et frimærke på mit **brev**.
sentence.en: I put a stamp on my letter.

et brud.explanation: "Et brud" means "a break or breach". To say a rule or agreement is not kept, use "et brud på" (a breach of): "et brud på aftalen" (a breach of the agreement). To talk about the end of a relationship, use the same word: "et brud mellem dem" (a break-up between them). Do not mix it up with "en brud" (a bride), which is an en-word: "Bruden smiler" (The bride smiles).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at der er et **brud** i foden.
sentence.en: The doctor says there is a fracture in the foot.

et brugernavn.explanation: "Et brugernavn" means "a username". It is built from "en bruger" (a user) and "et navn" (a name); "navn" is also in "et fornavn" (a first name).

sentence.da: Skriv dit **brugernavn** i feltet her.
sentence.en: Write your username in the field here.

et brusebad.explanation: "Et brusebad" means "a shower", as in washing yourself. To say you take one, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager et brusebad efter træning" (I take a shower after exercise).

sentence.da: Efter et **brusebad** er jeg ren og frisk.
sentence.en: After a shower I am clean and fresh.

et bruseforhæng.explanation: "Et bruseforhæng" means "a shower curtain". It is built from "bruse-" (shower) and "et forhæng" (a curtain).

sentence.da: Et **bruseforhæng** holder vandet væk fra gulvet.
sentence.en: A shower curtain keeps the water off the floor.

et bryggeri.explanation: "Et bryggeri" means "a brewery". It is built from "at brygge" (to brew).

sentence.da: Vi besøgte et **bryggeri** og smagte på den nye øl.
sentence.en: We visited a brewery and tasted the new beer.

et bryggers.explanation: "Et bryggers" means "a utility room". To say where the washing hangs, use "i bryggerset" (in the utility room): "Tøjet hænger i bryggerset" (The clothes are hanging in the utility room).

sentence.da: Vi har vaskemaskinen og fryseren i vores **bryggers**.
sentence.en: We have the washing machine and the freezer in our utility room.

et bryllup.explanation: "Et bryllup" means "a wedding". To say you are going to a wedding, use "til bryllup": "Vi skal til bryllup i morgen" (We are going to a wedding tomorrow).

sentence.da: Til et **bryllup** bærer bruden en hvid kjole.
sentence.en: At a wedding, the bride wears a white dress.

et bryst.explanation: "Et bryst" means "a chest", as in the front of the upper body. Danish says "brystet" (the chest) where English says "my chest": "Jeg har smerter i brystet" (I have pain in my chest). The word also means "a breast". To talk about the meat, use "et kyllingebryst" (a chicken breast).

sentence.da: Hjertet slår i mit **bryst**.
sentence.en: The heart beats in my chest.

et bræt.explanation: "Et bræt" means "a board", as in a flat piece of wood. To talk about more than one, use the plural "brædder": "tre brædder" (three boards). The word is also in "et strygebræt" (an ironing board).

sentence.da: Jeg saver et **bræt** over med en sav.
sentence.en: I saw a board in two with a saw.

et brætspil.explanation: "Et brætspil" means "a board game". It is built from "et bræt" (a board) and "et spil" (a game); "bræt" is also in "et skærebræt" (a cutting board).

sentence.da: I et **brætspil** flytter man brikker rundt på brættet.
sentence.en: In a board game you move pieces around on the board.

et bud.explanation: "Et bud" means "an offer or bid". To say what you think will happen, use it for a guess: "Mit bud er, at han kommer" (My guess is that he will come). To name a messenger, use it in "et cykelbud" (a bike courier).

sentence.da: Jeg har lagt et **bud** på huset, men det var for lavt.
sentence.en: I placed a bid on the house, but it was too low.

et budget.explanation: "Et budget" means "a budget". To say you keep to your plan for spending money, use "overholde" (keep to): "Vi overholder budgettet" (We stick to the budget).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **budget** til ferien.
sentence.en: We have a small budget for the vacation.

et budskab.explanation: "Et budskab" means "a message". Do not mix it up with "en besked" (a message). When you talk about the main point of a film, speech or ad, use "et budskab": "Hvad er budskabet i reklamen?" (What is the message of the ad?). When you talk about a note or text sent to someone, use "en besked": "Jeg har en besked til dig" (I have a message for you).

sentence.da: Filmens **budskab** er, at venskab er vigtigere end penge.
sentence.en: The film's message is that friendship is more important than money.

et bur.explanation: "Et bur" means "a cage". The word is also the last part of other words, such as "et fuglebur" (a birdcage) and "et hamsterbur" (a hamster cage).

sentence.da: Fuglen sidder i et **bur** med tremmer af metal.
sentence.en: The bird sits in a cage with metal bars.

et bureau.explanation: "Et bureau" means "an agency". In a travel word it is the last part of "et rejsebureau" (a travel agency). When you talk about furniture for clothes, it has a different meaning, "a dresser": "Tøjet ligger i bureauet" (The clothes are in the dresser).

sentence.da: Et **bureau** hjælper kunder med at planlægge rejser eller reklamer.
sentence.en: An agency helps customers plan trips or advertising.

et busstoppested.explanation: "Et busstoppested" means "a bus stop". It is built from "en bus" (a bus) and "et stoppested" (a place where something stops).

sentence.da: Jeg venter på bussen ved et **busstoppested**.
sentence.en: I am waiting for the bus at a bus stop.

et byggemarked.explanation: "Et byggemarked" means "a DIY store". It is built from "at bygge" (to build) and "et marked" (a market).

sentence.da: I et **byggemarked** kan du købe brædder, skruer og maling.
sentence.en: In a DIY store you can buy boards, screws and paint.

et byggeri.explanation: "Et byggeri" means "a construction", as in a building project. It comes from the verb "at bygge" (to build). When you talk about the whole building industry, it has a second meaning: "Hun arbejder i byggeriet" (She works in the building industry).

sentence.da: Et **byggeri** af et nyt hus tager ofte mange måneder.
sentence.en: Building a new house often takes many months.

et bytte.explanation: "Et bytte" means "prey". When you talk about trading one thing for another, it has a second meaning, "a swap": "Det var et godt bytte" (That was a good swap). It comes from the verb "at bytte" (to swap).

sentence.da: Ørnen styrter ned mod sit **bytte** i marken.
sentence.en: The eagle dives down toward its prey in the field.

et bål.explanation: "Et bål" means "a bonfire". In Denmark, people light bonfires on 23 June for Sankt Hans aften (Midsummer Eve): "Vi tænder et bål ved stranden" (We light a bonfire by the beach). Do not mix it up with "en brand" (a fire that destroys things): "Der er brand i huset" (The house is on fire).

sentence.da: Vi sidder rundt om et **bål** og griller pølser.
sentence.en: We sit around a bonfire and grill sausages.

et bånd.explanation: "Et bånd" means "a ribbon". When you talk about a close link between people, it means "a bond": "et stærkt bånd mellem søstre" (a strong bond between sisters). In "et lydbånd" (an audio tape), "bånd" means "tape".

sentence.da: Hun binder et rødt **bånd** om gaven.
sentence.en: She ties a red ribbon around the gift.

et bælt.explanation: "Et bælt" means "a strait". Denmark has two famous ones: "Storebælt" (the Great Belt) and "Lillebælt" (the Little Belt). Do not mix it up with "et bælte" (a belt for trousers), which has an extra e: "Jeg har et sort bælte" (I have a black belt).

sentence.da: Vandet mellem Fyn og Sjælland er et **bælt**.
sentence.en: The water between Funen and Zealand is a strait.

et bælte.explanation: "Et bælte" means "a belt". It is the last part of "et sikkerhedsbælte" (a seat belt), built from "sikkerhed" (safety). To tell someone to put on a seat belt, say: "Spænd sikkerhedsbæltet" (Fasten your seat belt).

sentence.da: Et **bælte** holder bukserne oppe.
sentence.en: A belt holds the trousers up.

et bær.explanation: "Et bær" means "a berry". Many berry names end in "bær", such as "et jordbær" (a strawberry) and "et blåbær" (a blueberry).

sentence.da: Et **bær** vokser på en busk og er ofte sødt.
sentence.en: A berry grows on a bush and is often sweet.

et bæst.explanation: "Et bæst" means "a beast". When you call a rough, unpleasant man a beast, you can say: "Han er et bæst" (He is a brute).

sentence.da: Et stort **bæst** med skarpe tænder gemte sig i skoven.
sentence.en: A big beast with sharp teeth hid in the forest.

et børneværelse.explanation: "Et børneværelse" means "a children's room". It is built from "børn" (children) and "et værelse" (a room). The start "børne-" means "children's" in other words too, such as "en børnebog" (a children's book).

sentence.da: Der er mange bamser i vores **børneværelse**.
sentence.en: There are many teddy bears in our children's room.
